1.1: Aight, so a bunch of folks already tried to write out what went down with everything that got fulfilled among us.
1.2: They got they info straight from the ones who saw it firsthand and been preachin' the word from jump.
1.3: I figured I'd do the same, since I been peepin' all this from the very start—I wanted to lay it out real proper for you, Theophilus.
1.4: So you can be sure about what you was taught and know it ain't no guesswork.
1.5: Back when Herod was king of Judea, there was this priest named Zacharias from the Abijah crew. His wife, Elizabeth, came from Aaron's bloodline too.
1.6: Both of 'em was solid folks—righteous in God's eyes, doin' all He asked, keepin' His rules, no funny business.
1.7: But they ain't have no kids, 'cause Elizabeth couldn't have none, and they was both gettin' up there in age.
1.8: One day, while Zacharias was on duty, servin' God like priests do,
1.9: It was his turn to go in the temple and burn incense, just like the tradition said.
1.10: A whole crowd was outside prayin' while he was doin' the incense thing.
1.11: Outta nowhere, an angel of the Lord showed up—posted on the right side of the incense altar.
1.12: Zacharias saw him and got shook—straight-up terrified.
1.13: But the angel said, "Chill, Zacharias. God heard your prayer. Your wife Elizabeth gon' have a son, and you gon' name him John.
1.14: He gon' bring you mad joy, and a lotta folks gon' celebrate when he's born.
1.15: This boy gon' be major in God's eyes. He ain't gon' drink no wine or strong liquor, and he gon' be full of the Holy Spirit even in the womb.
1.16: He gon' turn a whole lotta Israelites back to the Lord their God.
1.17: He gon' go ahead of the Lord, movin' like Elijah with power—gettin' fathers to reconnect with they kids, and rebellious folks to wise up—preppin' people for the Lord."
1.18: Zacharias said, "How I'm supposed to believe that? I'm old, and my wife ain't no spring chicken either."
1.19: The angel clapped back, "I'm Gabriel, fam. I stand in God's presence. He sent me to drop this good news to you.
1.20: But since you ain't believe me, you ain't gon' be able to talk till all this goes down—'cause what I said gon' happen at the right time."
1.21: Meanwhile, the people outside was waitin' on Zacharias like, "Why he takin' so long in there?"
1.22: When he finally came out, he couldn't talk. They realized he must've seen a vision, 'cause he was makin' hand signs and couldn't say a word.
1.23: Once his time workin' at the temple was up, he dipped back home.
1.24: Not long after, Elizabeth got pregnant. She laid low for five months.
1.25: She said, "Look what the Lord did for me. He saw me out here strugglin' and took away my shame."
1.26: Six months later, God sent Gabriel to a town in Galilee called Nazareth.
1.27: He came to a virgin named Mary. She was engaged to Joseph, a man from King David's bloodline.
1.28: Gabriel pulled up and said, "What's up, favored girl? The Lord's rockin' with you. You real blessed."
1.29: Mary got shook and was tryna figure out what this wild greeting even meant.
1.30: Gabriel said, "Don't be scared, Mary. You got God's favor for real.
1.31: You about to get pregnant and have a Son. Name Him Jesus.
1.32: He gon' be great—folks gon' call Him the Son of the Most High. God gon' give Him David's throne.
1.33: He gon' reign over Jacob's people forever, and His kingdom? It ain't never gon' end."
1.34: Mary said, "How that work? I ain't never been with no man."
1.35: Gabriel said, "The Holy Spirit gon' come over you, and God's power gon' cover you. That's why the child you havin' gon' be called the Son of God.
1.36: And check this—your cousin Elizabeth? She pregnant too, even in her old age. She six months in now—yeah, the same one folks said couldn't have no kids.
1.38: Mary said, "I'm down, Lord. Let it happen just like you said." And with that, the angel bounced.
1.39: Right after that, Mary got up and dipped out quick to the hill country in Judea.
1.40: She pulled up at Zacharias's crib and greeted Elizabeth.
1.41: Soon as Elizabeth heard Mary say hey, the baby in her belly jumped—and Elizabeth got filled up with the Holy Spirit.
1.42: She let out a loud shout and said, "Girl, you blessed for real! And the baby you carryin'? Blessed too!
1.43: But hold up—why I get this honor, that the mama of my Lord pulled up to see me?
1.44: 'Cause the second I heard your voice, my baby started dancin' inside me, full of joy.
1.45: You real blessed 'cause you believed what God said—and everything He promised you? It's comin' true."
1.46: Then Mary said, "My soul stay liftin' up the Lord.
1.47: My spirit is turnt up in God, my Savior.
1.48: He saw me when I was lowly and overlooked. From now on, everybody gon' call me blessed.
1.49: The Mighty One did somethin' major for me. His name holy for real.
1.50: He keeps showin' mercy to the ones that fear Him—generation after generation.
1.51: He showed out with His power—He scattered all them proud folks who thought they was somethin'.
1.52: He knocked rulers off they thrones, but lifted up the ones who was down bad.
1.53: He fed the hungry with the good stuff, but sent the rich home empty-handed.
1.54: He helped His people, Israel, just like He said He would.
1.55: He kept His promise to our ancestors—to Abraham and all his people forever."
1.56: Mary stayed with Elizabeth for about three months, then headed back to her own spot.
1.57: When it was time for Elizabeth to have her baby, she gave birth to a son.
1.58: Her neighbors and family heard how good the Lord had been to her, and they celebrated with her.
1.59: On the eighth day, they came to circumcise the baby. Folks was like, "Let's name him after his daddy—Zacharias."
1.60: But Elizabeth shut that down real quick: "Nah, his name gon' be John."
1.61: They was confused like, "Ain't nobody in your family named that."
1.62: So they turned to Zacharias, tryin' to get his take—askin' him what the baby's name should be.
1.63: He asked for a tablet and wrote: "His name is John." Everybody was shocked.
1.64: Right then, Zacharias could talk again—his mouth opened up, and he started praisin' God.
1.65: Everybody around there got shook. Word spread all over the hills of Judea about what went down.
1.66: Folks who heard about it kept it in their hearts, sayin', "What kinda child is this boy gon' be?" 'Cause clearly, God's hand was all over him.
1.67: Then Zacharias, filled with the Holy Spirit, started prophesyin', sayin':
1.68: "Bless the Lord, the God of Israel—He came through and saved His people.
1.69: He raised up a strong Savior from David's family line.
1.70: Just like He promised through His prophets from way back.
1.71: He savin' us from our enemies—from everybody that hate on us.
1.72: Showin' mercy like He told our ancestors, rememberin' that holy promise.
1.73: The oath He made to Abraham, our father:
1.74: That we'd be rescued from our enemies, so we could serve Him without fear.
1.75: Holy and righteous, standin' before Him every day of our lives.
1.76: And you, little one—you gon' be called the prophet of the Most High. You gon' go ahead of the Lord, makin' the way ready for Him.
1.77: You gon' teach His people how to be saved—how their sins can get wiped clean.
1.78: All 'cause our God is full of tender mercy. Heaven's light is breakin' in.
1.79: That light gon' shine on folks stuck in darkness and death's shadow. He gon' lead our steps right into peace."
1.80: The boy grew up strong in the Spirit, and he stayed out in the wilderness 'til the day he stepped out to show Israel who he was.

2.1: Back in the day, Caesar Augustus sent out a message sayin' everybody in the empire had to get registered.
2.2: This was the first census when Quirinius was runnin' Syria.
2.3: So everybody went to their hometown to sign up.
2.4: Joseph left Galilee, from the town of Nazareth, and headed down to Judea—to Bethlehem, David's hometown—'cause that's where his people came from.
2.5: He went to get registered with Mary, the one he was promised to, and she was pregnant.
2.6: While they was there, her time came to give birth.
2.7: She had her firstborn Son, wrapped Him up in cloth, and laid Him in a manger, 'cause there wasn't no room for them at the inn.
2.8: That same night, some shepherds was out in the fields nearby, watchin' over they sheep.
2.9: All of a sudden, an angel of the Lord showed up, and God's glory lit the whole place up—they was shook.
2.10: But the angel said, "Don't be scared. I got good news that's gon' bring joy to everybody.
2.11: Today, in David's city, a Savior been born for y'all—He the Messiah, the Lord.
2.12: Here's how you'll know it's Him: You'll find a baby wrapped up and layin' in a manger."
2.13: Then outta nowhere, a whole crew of heavenly angels popped up, praisin' God and sayin',
2.14: "Glory to God in the highest, and peace on earth to the ones He's pleased with!"
2.15: When the angels dipped back to heaven, the shepherds said, "Let's slide to Bethlehem and see what just happened—God really showed us somethin'."
2.16: They took off quick and found Mary, Joseph, and the baby—just like the angel said—layin' in the manger.
2.17: After they saw Him, they started tellin' everybody what the angel had said about this child.
2.18: Everybody who heard it was amazed at what the shepherds said.
2.19: But Mary held all this in her heart and kept thinkin' about it.
2.20: The shepherds went back praisin' and shoutin' to God for everything they saw and heard—just like it was told to them.
2.21: Eight days later, when it was time to circumcise the baby, they named Him Jesus—the name the angel gave before He was even in the womb.
2.22: After Mary's purification time was up—like the law of Moses said—they brought Jesus to Jerusalem to dedicate Him to the Lord.
2.23: (Just like the Scripture says: "Every firstborn male belongs to the Lord.")
2.24: They brought a sacrifice too—two doves or two young pigeons, like the law required.
2.25: There was a man in Jerusalem named Simeon. He was righteous and serious about God—waiting on God to comfort Israel. And the Holy Spirit was on him.
2.26: God had told him through the Spirit that he wouldn't die until he saw the Messiah.
2.27: The Spirit led him to the temple that day. And when Mary and Joseph brought in Jesus to do what the law required,
2.28: Simeon took the baby in his arms, praised God, and said:
2.29: "Lord, now You lettin' Your servant go in peace, just like You promised.
2.30: 'Cause my eyes done seen Your salvation
2.31: That You prepared for everybody to see—
2.32: A light for the non-Jews, and glory for Your people Israel."
2.33: Mary and Joseph were amazed at what he said about Jesus.
2.34: Simeon blessed them and told Mary, "This child gon' shake up a lotta folks in Israel. Some gon' rise, some gon' fall. And folks gon' speak against Him.
2.35: And girl, it's gon' hurt you too—like a sword to the soul. But in all that, people's hearts gon' be exposed."
2.36: There was a prophetess named Anna—daughter of Phanuel, from the tribe of Asher. She was old and had only been married seven years before her husband died.
2.37: She was now a widow, 84 years old, and never left the temple. She stayed worshipin'—fastin' and prayin' all day and night.
2.38: She walked up right when Simeon was speakin', thanked God, and told everybody waitin' for redemption in Jerusalem about that baby.
2.39: After they did everything God's law said to do, they went back home to Galilee—to the town of Nazareth.
2.40: The child grew up strong and full of wisdom—and God's grace was all over Him.
2.41: Every year, His folks went to Jerusalem for Passover.
2.42: When Jesus turned twelve, they took Him up there like they always did.
2.43: After the festival was over, they started headin' back home—but Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem. Joseph and Mary didn't even realize it.
2.44: They thought He was with the group, so they traveled a whole day before they started lookin' for Him among family and friends.
2.45: When they couldn't find Him, they rushed back to Jerusalem to look for Him.
2.46: Three days later, they found Him in the temple, sittin' with the teachers—listenin' and askin' questions.
2.47: Everybody that heard Him was blown away by His wisdom and the way He answered.
2.48: When His parents saw Him, they were shook. His mama said, "Son, why you do us like this? Me and your daddy been worried sick lookin' for you!"
2.49: Jesus said, "Why y'all lookin' for Me? Didn't y'all know I had to be in My Father's house, doin' His business?"
2.50: But they ain't really understand what He was sayin'.
2.51: Then He went back with them to Nazareth and obeyed them. But His mama kept thinkin' about everything that had happened.
2.52: And Jesus kept growin'—gettin' wiser, stronger, and more favored by God and people.

3.1: In the fifteenth year of Tiberius Caesar's rule, when Pontius Pilate was governor over Judea, Herod was over Galilee, his brother Philip was over Iturea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias ran things in Abilene.
3.2: While Annas and Caiaphas were the high priests, God's word came to John—Zacharias's son—out there in the wilderness.
3.3: He went all around the Jordan region preachin' a baptism that came with turnin' your life around and gettin' your sins wiped clean.
3.4: Just like the prophet Isaiah wrote: "Somebody's voice cryin' out in the wilderness, sayin', 'Get ready for the Lord to pull up! Make them paths straight!
3.5: Every valley gon' be lifted up, every mountain and hill brought low. What's crooked gon' get straight, and what's rough gon' smooth out.
3.6: And everybody—yeah, all flesh—gon' see God's salvation.'"
3.7: John looked at the crowds comin' to get baptized and said, "Y'all some snakes! Who warned y'all to run from the heat that's comin'?
3.8: If you really changin', show it in how you live. And don't start flexin' talkin' bout, 'We got Abraham as our daddy.' Let me tell you—God can make Abraham's kids outta these rocks if He wanted to.
3.9: The ax is already sittin' at the base of the tree. Any tree not bearin' good fruit? Gettin' chopped down and thrown in the fire."
3.10: The people said, "So what we s'posed to do?"
3.11: John said, "If you got two coats, give one to somebody who ain't got none. Same with food—share what you got."
3.12: Some tax collectors came through to get baptized and asked, "Teacher, what we need to do?"
3.13: He told 'em, "Don't take no more than what's owed. No skimming, no scamming."
3.14: Some soldiers asked too, "And us—what we gotta do?" He said, "Stop extorting folks, don't lie on nobody, and be cool with your paycheck."
3.15: Everybody was hyped, wonderin' if John might be the Messiah.
3.16: John said, "Look, I baptize with water, but somebody way stronger than me comin'. I ain't even worthy to untie His shoes. He gon' baptize y'all with the Holy Spirit and fire.
3.17: He got His winnowing fork ready to clear out the threshing floor—He gon' keep the wheat and burn the chaff with fire that don't go out."
3.18: John kept preachin' all kinds of real truth to the people, encouragin' 'em along the way.
3.19: But when he called out Herod for messin' with his brother Philip's wife, Herodias—and all the other wild stuff Herod had done—
3.20: Herod got petty and added one more thing to his mess: he locked John up in prison.
3.21: One day, while everybody was gettin' baptized, Jesus stepped up too. And while He was prayin', the sky opened up.
3.22: The Holy Spirit came down on Him like a dove, and a voice came from heaven sayin', "You My Son, My Beloved One—I'm proud of You."
3.23: Jesus was about thirty years old when He started His ministry. Folks thought He was Joseph's son. Joseph was the son of Heli,
3.24: Heli was the son of Matthat, son of Levi, son of Melchi, son of Janna, son of Joseph,
3.25: Son of Mattathiah, son of Amos, son of Nahum, son of Esli, son of Naggai,
3.26: Son of Maath, son of Mattathiah, son of Semei, son of Joseph, son of Judah,
3.27: Son of Joannas, son of Rhesa, son of Zerubbabel, son of Shealtiel, son of Neri,
3.28: Son of Melchi, son of Addi, son of Cosam, son of Elmodam, son of Er,
3.29: Son of Jose, son of Eliezer, son of Jorim, son of Matthat, son of Levi,
3.30: Son of Simeon, son of Judah, son of Joseph, son of Jonan, son of Eliakim,
3.31: Son of Melea, son of Menan, son of Mattathah, son of Nathan, son of David,
3.32: Son of Jesse, son of Obed, son of Boaz, son of Salmon, son of Nahshon,
3.33: Son of Amminadab, son of Ram, son of Hezron, son of Perez, son of Judah,
3.34: Son of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham, son of Terah, son of Nahor,
3.35: Son of Serug, son of Reu, son of Peleg, son of Eber, son of Shelah,
3.36: Son of Cainan, son of Arphaxad, son of Shem, son of Noah, son of Lamech,
3.37: Son of Methuselah, son of Enoch, son of Jared, son of Mahalalel, son of Cainan,
3.38: Son of Enosh, son of Seth, son of Adam, son of God.

4.1: Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, came back from the Jordan. The Spirit led Him straight into the wilderness.
4.2: He was out there forty days, gettin' tempted by the devil. He ain't eat nothin' that whole time. By the end, He was hungry for real.
4.3: The devil said, "If You really the Son of God, turn this stone into bread."
4.4: Jesus said, "Nah, it's written: Man can't live just off bread, but off every word God speaks."
4.5: Then the devil took Him up high, showed Him all the kingdoms of the world in a flash.
4.6: He said, "All this power and shine? I can give it to You. It was handed to me, and I can give it to whoever I want.
4.7: Bow down and worship me, and it's all Yours."
4.8: Jesus shot back, "Get behind Me, Satan. It's written: You only worship the Lord your God and serve Him only."
4.9: Then Satan took Him to Jerusalem, put Him on the highest part of the temple and said, "If You the Son of God, jump down!
4.10: 'Cause it's written: He gon' send angels to catch You,
4.11: And they'll hold You up so You don't even stub Your toe."
4.12: Jesus replied, "It also says: Don't test the Lord your God."
4.13: After Satan ran outta tricks, he dipped out—for now.
4.14: Jesus came back to Galilee powered up by the Spirit. Word about Him spread like wildfire through the whole area.
4.15: He was teachin' in the synagogues, and everybody was speakin' highly of Him.
4.16: He rolled up to Nazareth, where He grew up. Like He always did, He went to church on the Sabbath and stood up to read.
4.17: They handed Him the scroll of Isaiah. He found the spot that said:
4.18: "The Spirit of the Lord is on Me, 'cause He chose Me to bring good news to the broke folks. He sent Me to heal the heartbroken, To tell the captives they free, To give sight to the blind, To let the oppressed breathe easy,
4.19: And to declare that this is the year the Lord showin' up strong."
4.20: Then He closed the scroll, gave it back, and sat down. Everybody in the synagogue was starin' at Him.
4.21: He said, "Today, this scripture just came true while y'all was listenin'."
4.22: Everybody was stunned, like, "Wait—ain't this Joseph's boy? How He talkin' like that?"
4.23: Jesus said, "Y'all probably thinkin': 'Heal Yourself! Do the same stuff here You did in Capernaum.'"
4.24: He added, "No prophet gets love in his own hometown. Facts.
4.25: Back in Elijah's day, when no rain fell for three and a half years and there was a serious famine, there were plenty widows in Israel.
4.26: But Elijah wasn't sent to any of them—he went to a widow in Zarephath, way out in Sidon.
4.27: And in Elisha's day, there were lots of lepers in Israel, but the only one who got healed was Naaman—a Syrian."
4.28: That set everybody off in the synagogue. They were mad mad.
4.29: They jumped up, grabbed Him, and tried to drag Him out the city and throw Him off a cliff.
4.30: But Jesus just walked straight through 'em and kept it movin'.
4.31: Jesus went down to Capernaum, a town in Galilee, and taught on the Sabbath.
4.32: Folks were shocked—His words hit different. He had real authority.
4.33: While He was teachin', a man with a demon showed up in the synagogue and started yellin',
4.34: "Leave us alone! What You want with us, Jesus of Nazareth? You here to destroy us? I know who You are—the Holy One of God!"
4.35: Jesus shut him down quick: "Be quiet and get out!" The demon threw the man down and left him—but didn't hurt him.
4.36: Everybody was shook, like, "Yo! He got power and authority—He just tells demons what to do, and they obey!"
4.37: Word about Jesus spread everywhere around the region.
4.38: Jesus left the synagogue and went to Simon's house. His mother-in-law was real sick with a fever, and they asked Jesus to help.
4.39: He stood over her, spoke to the fever, and it left. She got up right away and started servin' them.
4.40: That night, as the sun was goin' down, folks brought all kinds of sick people to Him. Jesus laid hands on each one and healed them.
4.41: Demons came outta a lotta people, screamin', "You the Son of God!" But Jesus told 'em to hush—they knew He was the Christ, and He wasn't lettin' 'em spoil it yet.
4.42: Early next mornin', Jesus dipped out to a quiet spot. But the people came huntin' for Him, tryin' to make Him stay.
4.43: He told them, "I gotta spread the message about God's Kingdom to other towns too—that's why I was sent."
4.44: So He kept on preachin' in the synagogues all across Galilee.

5.1: One day, Jesus was standin' by the Lake of Gennesaret, and the crowd was pressin' in heavy, tryna hear God's word.
5.2: He saw two boats tied up at the shore, but the fishermen had stepped away and were washin' their nets.
5.3: Jesus hopped into one of the boats—it was Simon's—and asked him to push out a little from land. Then He sat down and started teachin' the crowd from the boat.
5.4: When He finished talkin', He told Simon, "Take it out deep and drop your nets. Let's catch somethin'."
5.5: Simon said, "Master, we been out here all night and ain't caught nothin'. But since You said it, I'ma drop the net."
5.6: When they did, the net filled up with so many fish it started breakin'.
5.7: They called out to their partners in the other boat for backup. Both boats got so full they started sinkin'.
5.8: When Simon Peter saw it, he dropped to Jesus' knees and said, "Lord, get away from me—I'm a sinful man."
5.9: He and everybody with him were shook by how many fish they caught.
5.10: James and John, sons of Zebedee—Simon's fishing partners—was shook too. But Jesus told Simon, "Don't be scared. From now on, you fishin' for people."
5.11: So they brought the boats back to shore, dropped everything, and followed Him.
5.12: In one town, a man full of leprosy saw Jesus. He fell on his face and begged, "Lord, if You willing, You can make me clean."
5.13: Jesus reached out, touched him, and said, "I'm willing. Be clean." Right then, the leprosy bounced.
5.14: Jesus told him, "Don't tell nobody. Go show yourself to the priest and make the offering Moses commanded, so folks know you really healed."
5.15: But word spread even more. Big crowds came to hear Him and get healed from whatever had them down.
5.16: But Jesus would dip off to quiet places often to pray.
5.17: One day, while Jesus was teachin', Pharisees and law teachers were sittin' there. They came from all over—Galilee, Judea, Jerusalem. And God's power was there, strong enough to heal.
5.18: Some folks showed up carryin' a man on a stretcher—he was paralyzed. They was tryna get him to Jesus.
5.19: But the crowd was too thick. So they went up on the roof, broke through the tiles, and lowered him right in front of Jesus.
5.20: When Jesus saw their faith, He said, "Man, your sins are forgiven."
5.21: The scribes and Pharisees started whisperin', "Who this man think He is? Only God can forgive sins!"
5.22: Jesus knew what they was thinkin'. He said, "Why y'all trippin' in your heads?
5.23: What's easier to say, 'Your sins forgiven,' or 'Get up and walk'?
5.24: But just so y'all know I got the authority to forgive sins down here..." He turned to the paralyzed man and said, "Get up, grab your mat, and go home."
5.25: Dude got up on the spot, grabbed what he was layin' on, and walked out praisin' God.
5.26: Everybody was buggin' out. They praised God and said, "We done seen some wild stuff today!"
5.27: After that, Jesus saw a tax man named Levi sittin' at his booth. Jesus said, "Follow Me."
5.28: Levi got up, left everything, and followed.
5.29: Then Levi threw a big dinner party for Jesus at his crib. A bunch of tax folks and other people pulled up too.
5.30: But the Pharisees and their crew were hatin', askin' Jesus' disciples, "Why y'all eatin' and drinkin' with these tax cheats and sinners?"
5.31: Jesus clapped back, "Healthy folks don't need no doctor—it's the sick ones who do.
5.32: I didn't come for the so-called righteous. I came for the sinners—to call them to turn they life around."
5.33: They asked Him, "Why do John's people fast and pray, and the Pharisees too, but Your people just eat and drink?"
5.34: Jesus said, "Can y'all make the wedding guests fast while the groom still there?
5.35: But the day gon' come when the groom gets taken away—then they gon' fast."
5.36: He hit them with a parable: "Ain't nobody patchin' old clothes with new fabric. The new piece gon' rip, and it won't even match.
5.37: And you don't pour new wine into old wineskins. If you do, the new wine gon' bust the skins, spill everywhere, and both get wasted.
5.38: You gotta put new wine in new wineskins.
5.39: But folks who used to the old wine don't want the new. They be like, 'The old hit better.'"

6.1: One Sabbath day, Jesus and His crew was walkin' through a grainfield. They started pickin' some heads of grain and rubbin' 'em in their hands to eat.
6.2: Some Pharisees saw it and said, "Why y'all doin' what ain't lawful on the Sabbath?"
6.3: Jesus clapped back, "Y'all ain't read what David did when he and his people were hungry?
6.4: He went into God's house, took the holy bread, ate it, and even gave some to his boys. That bread was only for the priests."
6.5: Then Jesus said, "The Son of Man is Lord—even over the Sabbath."
6.6: On another Sabbath, Jesus pulled up to the synagogue and started teachin'. A man with a messed-up right hand was there.
6.7: The Pharisees and law teachers were watchin' close, tryna catch Him slippin'—seein' if He'd heal on the Sabbath so they could accuse Him.
6.8: Jesus knew what they were on. He told the man, "Get up and stand in front of everybody." So dude stood up.
6.9: Then Jesus said, "Lemme ask y'all: On the Sabbath, is it right to do good or do harm? To save a life or destroy one?"
6.10: He looked around the room at all of them, then told the man, "Stretch out your hand." The man did, and his hand got healed—just like the other one.
6.11: The haters was heated. They started plottin' on what to do with Jesus.
6.12: Around that time, Jesus went up a mountain to pray. He was talkin' to God all night long.
6.13: When the sun came up, He gathered all His disciples and picked twelve of them to be apostles.
6.14: There was Simon (He called him Peter), Andrew (his brother), James, John, Philip, Bartholomew,
6.15: Matthew, Thomas, James (son of Alphaeus), Simon (called the Zealot),
6.16: Judas (son of James), and Judas Iscariot—the one who turned on Him.
6.17: Jesus came down with His crew and stood on a flat spot. A huge crowd from all over Judea, Jerusalem, and even coastal cities like Tyre and Sidon came through to hear Him and get healed.
6.18: People with sickness and those tormented by unclean spirits got healed.
6.19: Everybody was tryna touch Him, 'cause power was comin' outta Him and healin' everybody.
6.20: Jesus looked at His disciples and said: "Blessed are y'all who broke now—God's Kingdom belong to you.
6.21: Blessed are y'all who hungry now—God gon' fill you up. Blessed are y'all who cryin' now—laughter's comin'.
6.22: Blessed are you when folks hate on you, leave you out, trash your name, and lie on you 'cause of Me.
6.23: When that happens, be glad—jump for joy! Your reward in heaven gon' be big. They treated the prophets the same way."
6.24: "But woe to y'all who rich—you already got your comfort.
6.25: Woe to y'all who full now—you gon' be hungry. Woe to y'all who laugh now—you gon' mourn and cry later.
6.26: Woe when everybody speaks highly of you—that's what they did to the fake prophets."
6.27: "Look, I'm talkin' to the ones who really listen: Love your enemies. Do good to people who hate you.
6.28: Bless the ones that cuss you out. Pray for the folks who try to use you dirty.
6.29: If somebody slaps you on one cheek, offer the other. If they snatch your coat, let 'em have your hoodie too.
6.30: If somebody ask you for somethin', give it. If they take somethin' from you, don't chase it back.
6.31: However you want folks to treat you—do that for them too.
6.32: If you only love folks who love you—what's special about that? Even the worst folks do that.
6.33: If you only do good to people who do good to you—that ain't Kingdom. Sinners do that too.
6.34: If you only lend to people you know gon' pay back—what's that prove? Sinners lend to each other all the time.
6.35: But I'm tellin' you: love your enemies. Do good. Lend without expectin' nothin' back. Then your reward gon' be great, and you'll be kids of the Most High. 'Cause He's kind even to the shady and the ungrateful.
6.36: So be merciful—just like your Father is."
6.37: "Don't judge, and you won't get judged. Don't condemn, and you won't get condemned. Forgive, and you'll be forgiven.
6.38: Give, and it'll be given back to you—good measure, pressed down, shaken up, overflowin'. The same measure you use for others? That's what's comin' back to you."
6.39: He told them a parable: "Can a blind man lead another blind man? Nah—they both gon' end up in a ditch.
6.40: A student ain't above the teacher, but if he really learns, he'll be just like the teacher.
6.41: Why you so quick to point out the speck in your brother's eye, but got a whole plank in your own?
6.42: You say, 'Let me help you with that speck,' but you ain't checked your own plank? Hypocrite! Clean your own vision first—then you can see clear to help your brother."
6.43: "Good trees don't grow bad fruit. And bad trees don't grow good fruit.
6.44: You know a tree by the fruit it bears. Ain't nobody pickin' figs from thornbushes or grapes off a bramble bush.
6.45: A good heart brings out good things. A foul heart brings out foul things. Whatever's in the heart? That's what the mouth speaks."
6.46: "Why y'all callin' Me 'Lord, Lord' and don't do what I say?
6.47: If you come to Me, hear My words, and do them—I'll show you who that person's like:
6.48: They like somebody who built a house, dug deep, and laid the foundation on solid rock. When the flood came and the storm beat down, the house ain't even shake—it was locked in solid.
6.49: But the one who hears and don't act? They like somebody who built a house on dirt with no foundation. The storm hit, and the whole thing collapsed—big time."

7.1: After Jesus finished speakin' to the crowd, He headed into Capernaum.
7.2: There was a Roman officer who had a servant he really cared about, but the man was real sick and about to die.
7.3: When the officer heard about Jesus, he sent some Jewish elders to go ask Him to come and heal his servant.
7.4: When they got to Jesus, they begged hard: "This man deserves it, Lord.
7.5: He loves our people—and he even built us a synagogue."
7.6: So Jesus rolled with them. But before He got to the house, the officer sent some friends with a message: "Lord, don't trouble Yourself. I ain't even worthy to have You step in my house.
7.7: I didn't even feel right comin' to You myself. But if You just say the word, my servant gon' be healed.
7.8: I know how authority works—I'm under folks, and I got soldiers under me. I tell one, 'Go,' and he go. I tell another, 'Come,' and he show up. I say, 'Do this,' and it's done."
7.9: Jesus was blown away. He turned to the crowd and said, "Y'all, I ain't seen faith like this—not even in Israel."
7.10: And when the folks got back to the house, the servant was already healed.
7.11: The next day, Jesus went to a town called Nain. His disciples and a big crowd was rollin' with Him.
7.12: As He got close to the town gate, a funeral procession was comin' out. The dead man was the only son of his mama—and she was a widow. A big crowd was with her too.
7.13: When Jesus saw her, His heart broke. He said, "Don't cry."
7.14: He walked up and touched the coffin. The people carryin' it stopped. He said, "Young man, I'm talkin' to you—get up."
7.15: And just like that, the dead man sat up and started talkin'. Jesus handed him back to his mama.
7.16: Everybody was shook and started praisin' God: "A great prophet just pulled up!" and "God really came through for His people!"
7.17: Word spread fast—folks in Judea and all the surrounding areas were talkin' about it.
7.18: John's disciples told him everything Jesus was doin'.
7.19: So John called two of them and sent them to Jesus to ask, "Are You the One we been waitin' on? Or we gotta wait on somebody else?"
7.20: When they found Jesus, they said, "John the Baptist sent us to ask: 'Are You the One, or should we keep lookin'?'"
7.21: At that very moment, Jesus was healin' folks—people with diseases, demons, and blindness.
7.22: He told them, "Go tell John what y'all seen and heard: The blind see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead get up, and the poor hear good news.
7.23: And blessed is the one who ain't offended by Me."
7.24: After John's messengers left, Jesus turned to the crowd: "What y'all go out to the wilderness to see? A weak man swayin' in the wind?
7.25: A man in designer clothes? Nah—those kinda folks stay in royal mansions.
7.26: Y'all went out to see a prophet? Yep—and more than a prophet.
7.27: This the one the Scriptures talked about: 'I'm sendin' My messenger ahead of You, to get everything ready.'"
7.28: "I'm tellin' y'all—outta everybody born of a woman, ain't nobody greater than John. But even the least in God's kingdom is greater than him."
7.29: When the people heard that—including the tax collectors—they agreed with God's plan. They had been baptized by John.
7.30: But the Pharisees and law experts? They rejected God's will for them. They ain't even mess with John's baptism.
7.31: Jesus said, "What can I compare this generation to?
7.32: They like kids playin' in the street yellin' at each other, sayin': 'We played y'all a dance song, and you ain't dance. We sang sad songs, and you ain't cry.'
7.33: John the Baptist ain't eat bread or drink wine, and y'all said, 'He possessed!'
7.34: Then I show up eatin' and drinkin', and y'all say, 'Look at Him—greedy, always drinkin', hangin' with tax men and sinners.'
7.35: But wisdom proves herself by her actions—by her kids."
7.36: One of the Pharisees invited Jesus over for dinner. So He went and sat down at the table.
7.37: A woman in that city—everybody knew she was a sinner—heard He was there. She brought a jar of fancy perfume.
7.38: She stood behind Him cryin', her tears fallin' on His feet. She wiped them with her hair, kissed His feet, and poured the perfume on them.
7.39: The Pharisee who invited Him said to himself, "If this man was really a prophet, He'd know who that woman is and what kinda dirt she's done."
7.40: Jesus said, "Simon, lemme holler at you." Simon said, "Say it, Teacher."
7.41: "There was a man who loaned out money. One person owed him 500 coins, the other owed 50.
7.42: Neither could pay him back, so he forgave both. Which one you think gon' love him more?"
7.43: Simon said, "The one he forgave more." Jesus said, "You got that right."
7.44: Then He turned to the woman and said to Simon, "You see her? I came in your house, and you ain't offer Me no water to wash My feet. But she washed 'em with her tears and dried 'em with her hair.
7.45: You ain't kiss Me, but she ain't stopped kissin' My feet since I got here.
7.46: You ain't anoint My head, but she poured perfume on My feet.
7.47: That's why I'm tellin' you—her many sins? They forgiven. 'Cause she loved hard. But folks who think they barely need forgiveness barely show love."
7.48: Then He told the woman, "Your sins are forgiven."
7.49: The folks at the table started whisperin', "Who does He think He is—forgivin' sins?"
7.50: But Jesus told the woman, "Your faith saved you. Go in peace."

8.1: After that, Jesus started goin' from city to city and town to town, preachin' the good news about God's Kingdom. The twelve were rollin' with Him,
8.2: And so were some women He had healed from sickness and evil spirits—Mary Magdalene (she had seven demons cast outta her),
8.3: Joanna (wife of Chuza, who worked for King Herod), Susanna, and a bunch of other women who were helpin' take care of Him with their own money.
8.4: When a big crowd pulled up from all over, Jesus told a story:
8.5: "A farmer went out to throw some seeds. Some seeds landed on the sidewalk—they got stepped on or eaten by birds.
8.6: Some fell on rocky spots. They grew fast but dried up quick 'cause they ain't have no water.
8.7: Some landed in thorny bushes. The thorns grew up and choked them out.
8.8: But some fell on good ground—those ones grew and produced a harvest 100x over." Then Jesus yelled out, "If you got ears, then listen up!"
8.9: The disciples asked, "Jesus, what's that story really mean?"
8.10: He said, "Y'all gettin' the inside scoop on Kingdom mysteries. But for everybody else, I speak in stories—so even if they look, they don't see; and even if they hear, they don't get it."
8.11: "Let Me break it down: The seed? That's the word of God.
8.12: The ones that landed on the sidewalk? That's folks who hear the word, but then the devil snatches it away before they can believe and be saved.
8.13: The rocky ground? That's people who hear the word and get hype, but they don't got no roots. When life get hard, they fall off.
8.14: The thorns? That's folks who hear it, but they get caught up in life—bills, bags, and fun—and don't produce nothin'.
8.15: But the good soil? That's folks with a good, honest heart. They hear the word, hold on to it, and patiently produce good fruit."
8.16: "Nobody lights a lamp just to cover it up or stash it under the bed. You put it up high so people can see the light when they come in.
8.17: Ain't nothin' hidden that won't come to light. Whatever's done in secret? It's gon' show up.
8.18: So be careful how you listen. If you got it, more gon' be given. But if you ain't got it, even what you think you got gon' be taken."
8.19: Jesus' mama and brothers pulled up, but they couldn't get through 'cause of the crowd.
8.20: Somebody told Him, "Hey, Your mama and Your brothers outside tryna see You."
8.21: But Jesus said, "My real fam are the ones who hear God's word and actually live it out."
8.22: One day, Jesus got in a boat with His disciples and said, "Let's go to the other side." So they launched out.
8.23: While they were sailin', Jesus fell asleep. Then a storm hit the lake hard—the boat started fillin' with water. They were panickin'.
8.24: They woke Him up like, "Master, Master! We 'bout to die!" Jesus got up, checked the wind and the waves—and it all got still.
8.25: Then He looked at them and said, "Where y'all faith at?" They were shook and said, "Who is this man? Even the wind and water listen to Him!"
8.26: They landed in the Gadarenes, right across from Galilee.
8.27: As soon as Jesus stepped out the boat, a man with demons ran up. Dude had been possessed for years, wore no clothes, and lived in the cemetery.
8.28: When he saw Jesus, he screamed, dropped to his knees, and yelled, "What You want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? Don't torture me!"
8.29: (Jesus had already told the demon to come out. The man had been wildin'—they tried to chain him, but he'd break free every time and run out into the wild.)
8.30: Jesus asked, "What's your name?" The man said, "Legion"—'cause he had a whole army of demons inside.
8.31: The demons begged Jesus not to send them into the abyss.
8.32: There was a herd of pigs nearby. They begged to enter the pigs. Jesus said, "Go ahead."
8.33: The demons left the man, jumped in the pigs, and the whole herd ran off a cliff into the lake and drowned.
8.34: The pig herders ran off scared and told everybody in the town and countryside.
8.35: The crowd came out to see. They found the man who'd been possessed sittin' at Jesus' feet, dressed and in his right mind—and they got scared.
8.36: Folks who saw what happened explained the whole story.
8.37: The people from that region begged Jesus to leave—they were shook. So He got back in the boat.
8.38: The man who'd been healed begged to come with Him, but Jesus said,
8.39: "Go home. Tell everybody what God did for you." And dude went off tellin' his whole city what Jesus did for him.
8.40: When Jesus came back, the crowd was already waitin' on Him.
8.41: A man named Jairus—a synagogue leader—came fallin' at Jesus' feet, beggin' Him to come to his house.
8.42: His only daughter, about 12 years old, was dyin'. As Jesus was on His way, the crowd was pressin' up on Him.
8.43: A woman who had been bleeding for 12 years—spent all her money on doctors and still wasn't healed—
8.44: Came up from behind and touched the hem of His robe. Instantly, her bleeding stopped.
8.45: Jesus said, "Who touched Me?" Everybody denied it. Peter said, "Lord, the crowd's all over You. What You mean, 'Who touched Me?'"
8.46: Jesus said, "Nah—somebody touched Me for real. I felt power leave Me."
8.47: The woman realized she couldn't hide. She came trembling, fell at His feet, and told everybody what she did and how she got healed.
8.48: Jesus said, "Daughter, chill. Your faith healed you. Go in peace."
8.49: While He was talkin', someone from Jairus' house came and said, "Don't bother the Teacher no more—your daughter's dead."
8.50: Jesus heard it and said, "Don't be scared. Just believe. She gon' be alright."
8.51: When He got to the house, He only let Peter, James, John, and the girl's parents come inside.
8.52: Folks was cryin' and mournin', but Jesus said, "Stop cryin'. She ain't dead—she just sleepin'."
8.53: They laughed at Him, thinkin' He was trippin'—they knew she was gone.
8.54: But Jesus kicked them out, took her hand and said, "Little girl, get up."
8.55: Her spirit came back, and she stood up right away. He told them to get her somethin' to eat.
8.56: Her parents were stunned. But Jesus told 'em, "Keep this on the low."

9.1: Jesus called His twelve together and gave 'em the authority—power to cast out demons and heal the sick.
9.2: He sent them out to preach the Kingdom and heal anybody that needed it.
9.3: He told 'em, "Don't take nothin' for the trip—no staff, no bag, no food, no money. Don't even pack a second outfit."
9.4: "When you go into a house, stay there till you leave that city."
9.5: "If they don't receive you, brush that dust off your feet on the way out—as a sign against 'em."
9.6: So they hit the road, goin' from town to town, preachin' the good news and healin' folks everywhere.
9.7: Herod the tetrarch heard all the buzz about Jesus, and he was confused. Folks were sayin' John the Baptist was back from the dead,
9.8: Others said Elijah showed up, or maybe one of the old prophets came back.
9.9: Herod said, "I already had John killed… so who's this man makin' all this noise?" He tried to catch a glimpse of Jesus.
9.10: When the apostles came back, they told Jesus everything they did. He pulled them aside for some quiet time in a town called Bethsaida.
9.11: But the crowd wasn't tryna miss out—they followed Him. Jesus welcomed them, preached the Kingdom, and healed the sick.
9.12: Later in the day, the twelve said, "Jesus, send them folks away so they can find food and a place to stay. We out in the middle of nowhere."
9.13: But Jesus said, "Y'all give them somethin' to eat." They said, "We only got five loaves and two fish—unless you want us to go buy food for everybody." (It was about 5,000 men.)
9.14: Jesus told them, "Have the people sit down in groups of 50."
9.15: They did what He said, and everybody got seated.
9.16: Then Jesus took the five loaves and two fish, looked up to heaven, blessed the food, broke it, and gave it to the disciples to pass out.
9.17: Everybody ate till they was full—and they still picked up twelve baskets of leftovers.
9.18: One day while Jesus was prayin' alone, His disciples came through. He asked, "Who the crowd say I am?"
9.19: They said, "Some say John the Baptist, some say Elijah, others think one of the old prophets came back."
9.20: Jesus said, "But who do y'all say I am?" Peter said, "You the Christ. God's Chosen One."
9.21: Jesus told them not to tell nobody what Peter said.
9.22: He said, "The Son of Man gotta go through a lot—get rejected by the leaders, killed… but on the third day, He gon' rise."
9.23: Then He told them all, "If you wanna roll with Me, deny yourself. Pick up your cross daily, and follow Me.
9.24: If you try to save your life, you'll lose it. But if you lose your life for Me, you'll save it.
9.25: What good is it to gain the whole world, but lose your soul?
9.26: If you ashamed of Me and My words, I'll be ashamed of you when I come in glory with My Father and the angels.
9.27: But for real, some of y'all standin' here won't die till you see God's Kingdom show up."
9.28: About eight days later, Jesus took Peter, James, and John up a mountain to pray.
9.29: While He was prayin', His face changed and His clothes started glowin' white like lightning.
9.30: Two men showed up—Moses and Elijah—talkin' with Him.
9.31: They were radiant too, and talkin' about His soon-coming death in Jerusalem.
9.32: Peter and them was halfway sleep, but when they woke up, they saw Jesus in full glory and the two men with Him.
9.33: As Moses and Elijah started to leave, Peter said, "Uh… Jesus… maybe we should build three tents here—one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah." (He ain't really know what he was sayin'.)
9.34: While he was still talkin', a cloud came over them, and they got shook as it surrounded 'em.
9.35: A voice came from the cloud sayin', "This is My Son, My Chosen One—listen to Him!"
9.36: When the voice faded, Jesus was the only one there. The disciples kept quiet and ain't tell nobody what they saw—not yet.
9.37: The next day, when they came down the mountain, a big crowd met Jesus.
9.38: A man shouted from the crowd, "Teacher! Please look at my son—he's my only child!
9.39: A spirit takes control of him, he screams, foams at the mouth, and it barely ever lets him go—it's beatin' him up.
9.40: I asked Your disciples to cast it out, but they couldn't."
9.41: Jesus said, "Man, this generation got no faith and they wild. How long I gotta be patient with y'all? Bring the boy here."
9.42: While the boy was comin', the demon slammed him to the ground. Jesus checked the spirit, healed the boy, and gave him back to his daddy.
9.43: The crowd was amazed at God's power. While they were all still in awe, Jesus said to His disciples,
9.44: "Listen close—lock this in. The Son of Man is about to be betrayed."
9.45: But they ain't understand what He meant—it was hidden from them, and they were too scared to ask.
9.46: Then the disciples started arguin' about who was the greatest.
9.47: Jesus knew what they were thinkin'. He pulled a little child next to Him
9.48: And said, "Whoever welcomes this child in My name, welcomes Me. And whoever welcomes Me, welcomes the One who sent Me. The least one in the crew? That's the real MVP."
9.49: John said, "Master, we saw somebody castin' out demons in Your name and we told him to stop 'cause he ain't rollin' with us."
9.50: But Jesus said, "Don't stop him. If he ain't against us, he with us."
9.51: When the time came for Jesus to go to Jerusalem, He locked in and set His face that way.
9.52: He sent folks ahead to prepare a spot in a Samaritan village.
9.53: But they ain't mess with Him, 'cause He was headed to Jerusalem.
9.54: James and John saw that and said, "Lord, You want us to call fire down from heaven on them—like Elijah did?"
9.55: Jesus turned around and shut that down. "Y'all don't even know what kind of spirit you workin' with.
9.56: I ain't come to destroy people—I came to save 'em." So they just moved on to another town.
9.57: While they were walkin', someone said, "Jesus, I'll follow You wherever You go."
9.58: Jesus said, "Foxes got holes, birds got nests, but I ain't even got a place to lay My head."
9.59: He told another man, "Follow Me." The man said, "Let me go bury my father first."
9.60: Jesus said, "Let the dead bury they own dead. You got Kingdom business—go preach."
9.61: Another said, "Lord, I'll follow You, but let me say goodbye to my people first."
9.62: Jesus said, "If you start plowin' and keep lookin' back, you ain't built for the Kingdom."

10.1: After all that, Jesus picked 70 more folks and sent 'em out in pairs to every city He was headin' to.
10.2: He told 'em, "The harvest big, but ain't enough workers. So pray to the Lord of the harvest to send some folks out there."
10.3: "Now go on—I'm sendin' y'all out like sheep in the middle of wolves."
10.4: "Don't take no money, no bag, no shoes. And don't stop and chit-chat with folks on the road."
10.5: "When you walk in a house, say, 'Peace to this place.'"
10.6: "If there's peace in that house, it'll stay; if not, that peace gon' bounce right back to you."
10.7: "Stay in one house. Eat and drink what they give you, 'cause a worker deserve they pay. Don't be house-hoppin'."
10.8: "If you roll into a city and they welcome you, eat what they serve."
10.9: "Heal the sick there and let 'em know, 'The kingdom of God pulled up on y'all.'"
10.10: "But if that city don't want you? Step out into the street and say,
10.11: 'Even the dust from y'all town, we shakin' it off our feet. But just so y'all know—the kingdom still came through.'"
10.12: "And I'm tellin' you, on Judgment Day, Sodom gon' have it easier than that city."
10.13: "Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! If Tyre and Sidon saw what y'all saw, they woulda been cryin' and repentin' a long time ago."
10.14: "It's gon' be easier on Tyre and Sidon than on y'all."
10.15: "And you, Capernaum? Think you all the way up in heaven? Nah, you headed straight to the pit."
10.16: "Whoever listens to y'all, listens to Me. But whoever ignores y'all, ignores Me. And if they reject Me, they reject the One who sent Me."
10.17: The seventy came back hype, sayin', "Lord! Even demons got scared when we used Your name!"
10.18: Jesus said, "Yeah, I saw Satan drop like lightning outta heaven."
10.19: "I gave y'all the authority—y'all can step on snakes, scorpions, and walk over all the enemy's power. Ain't nothin' gon' hurt you."
10.20: "But don't get too caught up in spirits bowin' down to you. Be happy your names written in heaven."
10.21: Right then, Jesus got real joyful in the Spirit and said, "Thank You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth. You hid this from the so-called wise, but showed it to regular folks. That's how You wanted it."
10.22: "Everything the Father got, He handed to Me. Ain't nobody know who the Son really is but the Father—and nobody really know the Father 'cept the Son and whoever the Son wanna show Him to."
10.23: Then He looked at His disciples and said real low, "Y'all blessed to be seein' this."
10.24: "Prophets and kings been wishin' to see and hear what y'all gettin'—but they ain't."
10.25: A lawyer stood up tryin' to test Jesus: "Teacher, what I gotta do to get eternal life?"
10.26: Jesus said, "What's the law say? What you readin' in it?"
10.27: The man said, "Love God with all your heart, soul, strength, and mind—and love your neighbor like you love yourself."
10.28: Jesus said, "Bet. Do that, and you'll live."
10.29: But the man tryna save face asked, "Okay… so who count as my neighbor?"
10.30: Jesus broke it down: "A man was travelin' from Jerusalem to Jericho and got jumped—robbed, beat down, and left for dead."
10.31: "A priest came down the road, saw the man… and kept walkin' on the other side."
10.32: "Same thing with a Levite—he looked, then dipped to the other side."
10.33: "But a Samaritan—a man folks ain't even mess with like that—pulled up, saw him, and felt somethin' in his chest."
10.34: "He went to him, cleaned and bandaged his wounds with oil and wine, put him on his own ride, took him to an inn, and took care of him."
10.35: "Next day, he gave the innkeeper two coins and said, 'Take care of him. If it cost more, I'll handle it when I get back.'"
10.36: "Now which of the three was the real neighbor?"
10.37: The lawyer said, "The one who showed him mercy." Jesus said, "Exactly. Now go and do the same."
10.38: While Jesus was on His way, He came to a village where a woman named Martha welcomed Him into her house.
10.39: She had a sister named Mary, who sat at Jesus' feet, soakin' up everything He said.
10.40: But Martha was stressed—tryna serve and do all the things. She walked up on Jesus like, "Lord, You see me workin' by myself, right? Tell Mary to help me."
10.41: Jesus said, "Martha, Martha… you worried and stressed over a lot."
10.42: "But only one thing really matters. And Mary picked it. I ain't takin' that away from her."

11.1: One day while Jesus was prayin', when He finished, one of His disciples said, "Lord, teach us how to pray like John taught his crew."
11.2: So Jesus said, "When y'all pray, say: 'Father in heaven, we lift Your name up high. Let Your kingdom come, And Your will go down here on earth, just like it is up there.'"
11.3: "Give us what we need today to make it through."
11.4: "And forgive us for the wrong we done, 'Cause we forgivin' everybody who done us dirty. Don't let us get caught slippin' into temptation, And keep us safe from the evil one."
11.5: Then He said, "Say one of y'all got a friend, and at midnight you show up at his door like, 'Bro, lemme get 3 loaves of bread.'
11.6: "'I got a guest who just pulled up, and I ain't got nothin' for him.'"
11.7: "And your boy inside like, 'Man, don't bother me. The door locked, kids sleepin', I ain't gettin' up.'"
11.8: "But I'm tellin' you—he might not get up 'cause y'all tight, but if you keep knockin'? He gon' get up and give you whatever you need."
11.9: "So I'm tellin' y'all—ask and it'll be given. Seek and you'll find. Knock and the door gon' open."
11.10: "Everybody who asks gets it. Whoever seeks, finds. Whoever knocks, the door opens."
11.11: "If your son ask for bread, you gon' give him a rock?"
11.12: "Or if he ask for fish, you handin' him a snake?"
11.13: "Or he ask for an egg, you gon' give him a scorpion? Nah."
11.14: "So if y'all—who got issues—still know how to give your kids good gifts, how much more your heavenly Father gon' give the Holy Spirit to those who ask?"
11.15: Jesus cast out a demon that made somebody mute. When the demon left, the person could talk again. Everybody was shook.
11.16: But some haters said, "He castin' out demons with Beelzebub power."
11.17: Jesus, knowin' they thoughts, said, "A kingdom beefin' with itself gon' fall. A house that's divided? It's done for."
11.18: "If Satan fightin' Satan, his whole setup fallin' apart. But y'all say I'm castin' demons out with Beelzebub?"
11.19: "If that's true, who your people castin' demons out by? They gon' judge y'all."
11.20: "But if I'm castin' demons out with God's finger? Then y'all better know the Kingdom of God just touched down."
11.21: "When a strong man strapped up guards his stuff, it's safe."
11.22: "But if somebody stronger roll up, beat him down, and take his gear? He divvyin' up the loot."
11.23: "If you ain't with Me, you against Me. If you ain't helpin' Me gather, you just scatterin'."
11.24: "When a dirty spirit leave somebody, it roam through dry places lookin' for rest. If it can't find none, it say, 'Lemme go back to the crib I left.'"
11.25: "When it get back and see the place all swept and tidy…"
11.26: "It go get seven more demons, even worse, and they move in. That person end up worse than they started."
11.27: While Jesus was talkin', a woman in the crowd shouted, "Blessed is the woman who carried You and fed You!"
11.28: But Jesus said, "Even more blessed is the one who hear God's word and live it out."
11.29: When the crowd got thick, Jesus said, "This generation? Y'all wild. Always wantin' a sign. The only one you gettin' is Jonah."
11.30: "Jonah was a sign to Nineveh. Same way, the Son of Man is a sign to y'all."
11.31: "The Queen of the South gon' rise up at judgment and call this generation out. She traveled far just to hear Solomon. And I'm greater than Solomon."
11.32: "Nineveh gon' rise up too. They repented when Jonah preached. And I'm greater than Jonah."
11.33: "Ain't nobody light a lamp then hide it. Nah—they put it where folks can see."
11.34: "Your eye is the lamp to your body. If your eye right, your whole body lit up. If your eye messed up, you walkin' in the dark."
11.35: "So be careful the light you think you got ain't really darkness."
11.36: "If your whole self lit with no dark spots, you gon' shine like a lamp glowin' in a dark room."
11.37: While He was speakin', a Pharisee asked Jesus to come eat. So He went in and sat down.
11.38: The Pharisee peeped that Jesus ain't wash up before eatin', and he was lowkey judgin'.
11.39: Jesus said, "Y'all Pharisees got the outside lookin' clean, but inside? Greedy and grimy."
11.40: "Y'all fools—didn't the same One who made the outside make the inside too?"
11.41: "Instead of lookin' clean, be generous from the heart. Then everything gon' be clean for real."
11.42: "Woe to y'all Pharisees! Y'all be tithin' spices but forget justice and God's love. You should've done both."
11.43: "Woe to y'all who love front-row synagogue seats and attention in the streets."
11.44: "Woe to y'all! Y'all like hidden graves—folks walk over you and don't even know they touchin' death."
11.45: One of the lawyers spoke up: "Hold on, Jesus—you roastin' us too."
11.46: Jesus said, "Oh, I got heat for y'all too! Y'all put heavy weights on folks' backs but won't lift a finger to help."
11.47: "Woe to y'all! Y'all build tombs for the prophets your folks murdered."
11.48: "You basically cosignin' they murders. They killed the prophets, and y'all decoratin' the graves."
11.49: "That's why God said, 'I'ma send prophets and apostles—but y'all gon' kill and harass them too.'"
11.50: "So all that blood, from the first prophet to the last, is on this generation."
11.51: "From Abel to Zechariah—yeah, I said it—it's comin' down on y'all."
11.52: "Woe to y'all lawyers! Y'all stole the keys to truth. You ain't goin' in, and you blockin' folks tryin' to."
11.53: After all that, the scribes and Pharisees came at Jesus hard, grillin' Him from every angle.
11.54: They was watchin' for Him to slip up, tryin' to trap Him in His words so they could bring charges.

12.1: Around that time, a crowd so big it was damn near stampedin' folks gathered up. Jesus looked at His people first and said, "Y'all watch out for that Pharisee spirit—that fake holy actin'. That's straight-up hypocrisy."
12.2: "Ain't nothin' gonna stay hidden forever. What's done in the dark? It's gon' come to light."
12.3: "What you whisperin' behind closed doors? That's gon' be shouted from the rooftops. Don't get it twisted."
12.4: "Listen, fam—don't be scared of folks who can only kill the body. That's all they can do. That's it."
12.5: "Let me tell you who you should fear—fear the One who can put your soul in hell after this life. Yeah, I said it. Fear Him."
12.6: "Ain't five little birds sold for two pennies? But God don't forget not even one of 'em."
12.7: "Shoot, God even know how many hairs on your head! So stop worryin'. You worth way more than a flock of birds."
12.8: "Look, if you stand up for Me in front of folks, I'ma stand up for you in front of the angels."
12.9: "But if you act like you don't know Me? I'ma do the same up there. Don't play."
12.10: "Now if somebody talk down on the Son of Man, they can get forgiveness. But anybody speakin' wild 'bout the Holy Ghost? Ain't no forgiveness comin'."
12.11: "When they drag y'all to court or try to press y'all in them synagogues, don't stress 'bout what to say."
12.12: "The Holy Spirit gon' coach you in the moment. You'll know exactly what to say when the time hit."
12.13: Then somebody in the crowd yelled out, "Jesus! Tell my brother to split our daddy's inheritance with me!"
12.14: Jesus was like, "Bruh… who made Me the judge or lawyer between y'all?"
12.15: He turned to the crowd and said, "Watch out! Don't be greedy! Life ain't about stacking stuff up. That ain't where the real value at."
12.16: Then He told a parable: "A rich man had a whole bunch of crops come in."
12.17: "He thought to himself, 'Whew! I don't even got space for all this.'"
12.18: "So he said, 'I know! I'ma tear down my barns and build bigger ones. Then I'll store up everything nice and neat.'"
12.19: "He said, 'Soul, we good! Time to chill—eat, drink, and kick back.'"
12.20: "But God came through like, 'Fool! You dyin' tonight. Then what? Who all that stuff gon' belong to?'"
12.21: "That's what it's like for folks who hoard riches for themselves but don't invest in God's kingdom. Empty flex."
12.22: Then Jesus turned to His disciples and said, "Stop stressin' about your life—what you gon' eat, or your body—what you gon' wear."
12.23: "Life is more than food. Your body got more purpose than clothes."
12.24: "Look at the ravens—they don't farm or stack food, but God feeds them. You more valuable than some birds, right?"
12.25: "Tell me—who can grow an inch by worryin' 'bout it?"
12.26: "If worry can't do the small stuff, what you trippin' for on the big stuff?"
12.27: "Check out the lilies. They ain't workin', they ain't spinning thread, but I'm tellin' you—Solomon in his finest wasn't even touchin' 'em."
12.28: "So if God clothes the grass like that—grass that's here today and tossed in the fire tomorrow—don't you think He got you, too? Where your faith at?"
12.29: "Stop chasin' food and drink like you desperate. Don't let your mind stay in panic mode."
12.30: "All the nations stay pressed about that stuff. But your Father know what you need."
12.31: "You focus on God's kingdom first, and everything else gon' follow."
12.32: "Don't be scared, little flock—your Father wants to give you the kingdom."
12.33: "Sell what you got and give to folks in need. Stack heavenly bread that don't run out, that moths can't eat and nobody can steal."
12.34: "Where your treasure at? That's where your heart gon' be too."
12.36: "Be like folks waitin' on their boss to come back from a wedding. So when he knock, y'all ready to open that door immediately."
12.37: "Blessed—blessed—is the one who's stayin' on point, watchin' for the Master. I'ma tell y'all straight up, when He come back and see them on they job? He gon' put on the apron, sit them down, and He gon' serve them. Wild, right?"
12.38: "Even if He show up in the late-night hours—second watch, third watch—and still finds them ready? Yep, still blessed."
12.39: "Just know this: if the man of the house knew what time a thief was comin', he'd be up, locked and loaded, not lettin' nobody break in."
12.40: "That's why you gotta stay ready too. 'Cause the Son of Man gon' show up when you least expect Him."
12.41: Peter asked, "Lord, you talkin' to just us or everybody?"
12.42: Jesus said, "Let me ask you—who is that real one? The faithful and wise one the Master puts in charge to make sure the whole crew eats at the right time?"
12.43: "That servant, if he's still doin' the job when the Master returns? Blessed."
12.44: "Straight up, the Master gon' trust him with everything."
12.45: "But if that servant start wildin'—thinkin' 'The Master takin' His sweet time,' and he start beatin' folks, actin' reckless, partyin', and drinkin'—"
12.46: "The Master gon' pull up unannounced, catch him slippin', and it's a wrap. He gettin' cut off, sent out with the fakes."
12.47: "That servant who knew what the Master expected but ain't prepare? He gettin' beat down bad."
12.48: "But the one who didn't know, and still messed up? Lighter punishment. 'Cause look—when God gives you a lot, He expects a lot back. If you been entrusted with much? Best believe you gon' be held accountable."
12.49: "Y'all think I came to light candles and sing 'Kumbaya'? Nah. I came to light fire on this earth—and I wish it was already lit!"
12.50: "But first, I got a baptism to go through—and I'm heavy about it till it's done."
12.51: "Y'all really think I came to bring peace on earth? No sir, no ma'am—I came to divide."
12.52: "From now on, even houses gon' be split—three on this side, two on that."
12.53: "Fathers and sons at odds. Mamas and daughters bumpin' heads. In-laws beefin'. My presence exposes the real."
12.54: Then Jesus turned to the crowd: "Y'all can read the weather—see a cloud and say, 'Rain's comin',' or feel the wind and know it's gon' be hot."
12.55: "And y'all right when you do that!"
12.56: "But hypocrites—how you readin' the sky better than you readin' the signs of this time? Make it make sense."
12.57: "Why y'all waitin' on courts to settle every little thing? You know what's right—do it."
12.58: "If somebody got beef with you, try to squash it before y'all get to court. 'Cause once the judge get involved? You might end up in jail."
12.59: "And I'm tellin' you—you ain't gettin' out till you pay every single cent. Period."

13.1: Some folks pulled up and told Jesus 'bout some Galileans Pilate had killed while they was makin' sacrifices.
13.2: Jesus said, "Y'all think them Galileans was worse sinners than the rest 'cause that happened to 'em?"
13.3: "Nah. I'm tellin' y'all, unless you turn your life around, you gon' perish too."
13.4: "What 'bout them 18 folks that got crushed when that tower in Siloam fell—y'all think they was worse than everybody else in Jerusalem?"
13.5: "Nope. I'm tellin' you again, if you don't repent, you gon' perish just the same."
13.6: Then He dropped a parable: "There was a man who had a fig tree planted in his vineyard. He came lookin' for fruit and ain't find nothin'."
13.7: "He told the gardener, 'I been checkin' this tree for three years now. Ain't no fruit. Chop it down—it's just takin' up space.'"
13.8: "But the gardener said, 'Hold up, boss. Give it one more year. Let me dig around it and throw some fertilizer on it.'"
13.9: "'If it grow fruit next year, cool. If not, then go ahead and cut it down.'"
13.10: One Sabbath, Jesus was teachin' at the synagogue.
13.11: And there was a woman in there who'd been hunched over with a spirit of sickness for 18 years—she couldn't even stand up straight.
13.12: Jesus saw her, called her over and said, "Ma'am, you free from that sickness now."
13.13: Then He laid His hands on her, and boom—she stood up straight and started praisin' God.
13.14: But the synagogue leader was big mad 'cause Jesus healed on the Sabbath. He told the crowd, "Y'all got six days to get healed—don't be comin' here on the Sabbath for that."
13.15: Jesus clapped back: "You a hypocrite! Don't all y'all untie your ox or donkey on the Sabbath to take it to get some water?"
13.16: "So why can't this woman—this daughter of Abraham—who's been tied up by Satan for 18 years, get set free on the Sabbath too?"
13.17: After He said that, all His haters got real quiet. But the people? They was lovin' it—celebratin' everything He did.
13.18: Then Jesus asked, "What can I compare God's kingdom to?"
13.19: "It's like a mustard seed a man planted in his garden. It grew big and turned into a tree, and birds came and chilled in its branches."
13.20: Then He asked again, "What else can I compare God's kingdom to?"
13.21: "It's like some yeast a woman mixed into three batches of dough—just a lil bit—but it spread till the whole thing rose up."
13.22: Jesus kept it movin', teachin' in towns and villages on His way to Jerusalem.
13.23: Somebody asked Him, "Lord, is it only a few that's gonna get saved?" He said,
13.24: "Y'all better fight to get through the narrow door, 'cause a lot gon' try and still won't make it."
13.25: "Once the Master gets up and locks the door, y'all gon' be bangin' on it like, 'Lord, let us in!' But He gon' say, 'I don't know y'all. Where you from?'"
13.26: "Then y'all gon' say, 'We ate with You, You taught in our streets!'"
13.27: "And He still gon' say, 'I don't know you. Get outta here, all y'all doin' evil.'"
13.28: "There's gon' be cryin' and teeth-grindin' when y'all see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets sittin' pretty in God's kingdom—while you get left out."
13.29: "Folks gon' come from the east, west, north, and south, and sit at the table in God's kingdom."
13.30: "And just so you know—the last gon' be first, and the first gon' be last."
13.31: That same day, some Pharisees told Him, "You should dip. Herod tryin' to kill You."
13.32: Jesus said, "Go tell that fox I'm busy—castin' out demons and healin' folks today and tomorrow. And on the third day, I'll be done."
13.33: "But for real, I gotta keep movin'. A prophet don't go out like that anywhere but Jerusalem."
13.34: "Jerusalem, Jerusalem! You the city that kills prophets and stones the ones God sends. I been wantin' to scoop y'all up like a mama hen with her chicks under her wings—but y'all ain't want that."
13.35: "Now look—your house is left empty. And I'm tellin' you this: you won't see Me again till you say, 'Blessed is the One who comes in the name of the Lord!'"

14.1: One Sabbath, Jesus went to go eat at this Pharisee leader's house, and folks was watchin' Him real close.
14.2: And there was a man there in front of Him who had dropsy—body was all swollen up.
14.3: Jesus looked at the lawyers and Pharisees and said, "Y'all tell me—is it cool to heal on the Sabbath or not?"
14.4: They ain't say nothin'. So Jesus healed the man, and let him go on.
14.5: Then Jesus asked, "Which one of y'all wouldn't pull your donkey or ox out the ditch if it fell in on the Sabbath?"
14.6: They still ain't have nothin' to say.
14.7: Jesus noticed how everybody was tryin' to grab the best seat at the dinner, so He dropped this parable on them.
14.8: He said, "When somebody invites you to a wedding, don't go sittin' in the fanciest seat. Somebody more important might show up."
14.9: "Then the host gon' have to come tell you, 'Hey, give that seat to this person,' and you gon' have to slide to the back embarrassed."
14.10: "Instead, when you show up, sit in the lowest spot. Then the host might come up like, 'Friend, come sit up front,' and boom—you look good in front of everybody."
14.11: "Anybody tryna big themselves up gon' get humbled. But if you stay humble, God gon' lift you up."
14.12: Then Jesus told the host, "Next time you throw a party, don't just invite your crew, your cousins, and folks who got money to invite you back."
14.13: "Instead, invite folks who broke—folks who crippled, folks who blind, folks who can't walk."
14.14: "You gon' be blessed 'cause they can't pay you back. But God gon' pay you back at the resurrection of the righteous."
14.15: Somebody at the table heard Jesus and said, "Man, blessed is the one who gets to eat in God's kingdom."
14.16: Jesus said, "Let me tell you somethin'. A man was throwin' a big dinner and invited a bunch of folks."
14.17: "When it was time to eat, he sent his servant out sayin', 'Come on, y'all—it's ready.'"
14.18: "But everybody started makin' excuses. One said, 'I just bought some land, gotta go check it out.'"
14.19: "Another said, 'I got five oxen I just bought—I need to go test 'em out.'"
14.20: "Another said, 'I just got married, so I can't come.'"
14.21: "The servant came back and told the master. The master got mad and told him, 'Go out in the streets and alleys—bring in the poor, the crippled, the blind, and the lame.'"
14.22: "The servant said, 'I did that already—and there's still room.'"
14.23: "So the master said, 'Alright, go out to the highways and back roads—make 'em come in. I want this house full!'"
14.24: "'And I promise you—none of them folks who was originally invited gon' get a bite of this food.'"
14.25: Big crowds was followin' Jesus, so He turned and said somethin' real.
14.26: "If you come to Me but love your mama, daddy, wife, kids, brothers, sisters—or even your own life—more than Me, you can't be My disciple."
14.27: "If you ain't willin' to carry your own cross and follow Me, you ain't ready."
14.28: "Think about it—if you tryna build a tower, don't you sit down first and count the cost to make sure you got enough to finish it?"
14.29: "Otherwise, if you start buildin' and can't finish, everybody gon' laugh at you."
14.30: "They gon' say, 'Look at this dude—started buildin' and couldn't even finish!'"
14.31: "Or say a king wanna go to war with another king—don't he sit down and think, 'Can I beat this other king with 10,000 troops if he got 20,000?'"
14.32: "If not, he gon' send folks ahead of time to work out peace before the fight even start."
14.33: "Same goes for y'all—if you ain't ready to give up everything, you can't be My disciple."
14.34: "Salt is good—but if it loses its flavor, how you gon' make it salty again?"
14.35: "It ain't good for the soil or even the trash pile. Folks just throw it out. If you got ears, listen up."

15.1: All the tax collectors and folks known for wild livin' came close to hear Jesus talk.
15.2: But the Pharisees and scribes was hatin', talkin' bout, "Look at Him—He be chillin' with sinners and even eats with 'em."
15.3: So Jesus hit 'em with a parable, sayin:
15.4: "If one of y'all got a hundred sheep and one goes missin', don't you leave the other ninety-nine in the wilderness and go lookin' for that lost one 'til you find it?"
15.5: "And when you find it, you happy as ever—pickin' it up, throwin' it over your shoulders, feelin' real good."
15.6: "Then when you get home, you call your folks and neighbors like, 'Y'all celebrate with me—I found my lost sheep!'"
15.7: "Same way, I'm tellin' y'all—heaven turnin' up over one sinner who repents more than over ninety-nine folks who think they don't need to."
15.8: "Or say a woman got ten silver coins, and she lose one. Ain't she gon' light a lamp, sweep the whole house, and search like crazy 'til she finds it?"
15.9: "And when she do find it, she gon' call her girls and say, 'Turn up with me, I done found my lost coin!'"
15.10: "I'm tellin' y'all again—angels in heaven celebratin' when one sinner turns their life around."
15.11: Then Jesus kept goin': "A man had two sons."
15.12: "The younger one told his daddy, 'Pops, let me get my share of the inheritance now.' So the father split up the assets."
15.13: "Not long after that, the younger son packed all his stuff and dipped out to a far-off place. He wilded out and blew all his money on reckless livin'."
15.14: "When he ran outta funds, a real bad famine hit that land, and he was down bad."
15.15: "So he got a job with some man out there who sent him to the fields to feed pigs."
15.16: "He was so hungry, he was lookin' at pig slop like it was a five-star meal. But nobody gave him nothin'."
15.17: "Then he came to his senses and said, 'Wait—my daddy's hired workers eat good every day, and I'm out here starvin'?'"
15.18: "'I'ma get up, go back home, and say, "Daddy, I messed up against heaven and against you."'"
15.19: "'"I don't even deserve to be called your son no more. Just hire me like one of your workers."'"
15.20: "So he got up and headed home. But when he was still a long ways off, his daddy saw him, got moved with compassion, ran to him, hugged him up, and kissed him."
15.21: "The son said, 'Daddy, I've sinned against heaven and you. I'm not worthy to be your son no more.'"
15.22: "But his father told the servants, 'Quick! Go get the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his hand and some sandals on his feet.'"
15.23: "'Kill that fattened calf we been savin'—we throwin' a feast. Time to celebrate.'"
15.24: "'My boy was dead, now he alive. He was lost, now he found.' And they got the party started."
15.25: "Meanwhile, the older son was out in the field. When he came near the house, he heard music and folks dancin'."
15.26: "He asked one of the servants what was goin' on."
15.27: "The servant said, 'Your brother came back, and your pops killed the fattened calf 'cause he made it back safe.'"
15.28: "But the older brother got mad and wouldn't go in. So his father came out tryna talk him into it."
15.29: "He said, 'Look—I been grindin' for you all these years. I always did what you said. And you never even gave me a lil' goat to celebrate with my crew.'"
15.30: "'But this dude—your son—he wasted your money on prostitutes and wildin', and now you givin' him the royal treatment?'"
15.31: "The father said, 'Son, you been with me this whole time, and everything I got is yours.'"
15.32: "'But we had to celebrate. Your brother was dead, now he alive. He was lost, now he found.'"

16.1: Jesus turned to His disciples and said, "So check this out: there was this rich man who had a manager. Word got back to him that dude was blowin' his money recklessly.
16.2: So the boss called him in like, 'What's this I'm hearin'? Run me them numbers—you fired.'
16.3: The manager was like, 'Man, what I'ma do now? I ain't built for hard labor, and I got too much pride to be out here beggin.'
16.4: Then he got slick with it: 'I know! I'ma make some moves so folks still look out for me after I'm out this job.'"
16.5: So he started callin' up everybody who owed the boss money. He told the first dude, 'How much you owe?'
16.6: Dude said, 'A hundred gallons of oil.' He said, 'Cool, cut that down to fifty.'
16.7: Then the next one owed wheat—he said, 'Take it from a hundred to eighty.'
16.8: The rich man peeped it and, surprisingly, was like, 'Okay… that was lowkey clever.' Jesus said, "Look, the people of the world be movin' smarter sometimes than God's own people."
16.9: "So here's the takeaway: Use money wisely now—even shady money—'cause when it runs out, it can open eternal doors.
16.10: Whoever faithful with little will be faithful with much. But if you dirty with the small stuff? Don't expect promotion.
16.11: If you can't be trusted with money, how God gon' trust you with spiritual wealth?
16.12: If you messy with what ain't yours, who gon' give you what is yours?
16.13: You can't serve two bosses. You either ride for God or ride for the bag. Can't do both."
16.14: Now the Pharisees heard all this, and they were clowned up 'cause they loved money. So they started sneerin' at Jesus.
16.15: But Jesus clapped back: "Y'all always tryna make yourselves look good in front of folks—but God see your hearts. What looks flashy to man be foul to God."
16.16: "God's law been preached since Moses and the prophets. John came, and now everybody tryna squeeze into the kingdom.
16.17: But just know—God's Word ain't changin'. Not even a lil' accent mark gone fade away.
16.18: And oh yeah—divorcin' your wife just to marry somebody else? That's adultery. Same if you marry someone who already divorced."
16.19: "Now lemme tell y'all a real one: There was this rich man—draped in purple, livin' large every day.
16.20: Meanwhile, outside his gate, laid Lazarus—a broke man full of sores.
16.21: All he wanted was crumbs off the rich man's table. The dogs had more sympathy than the man—they licked his wounds.
16.22: One day, Lazarus died and angels carried him to chill with Abraham. The rich man died too—and ended up in hell, in flames.
16.23: From the heat, he looked up and saw Abraham and Lazarus far away, in peace.
16.24: He shouted, 'Father Abraham! Please send Lazarus to dip his finger in some water and cool my tongue—I'm burnin' down here!'
16.25: Abraham said, 'Remember, son, you had it good in your life. Lazarus had it rough. Now it's his turn for rest and yours for regret.
