16.26: And besides, there's a huge gap between us. Nobody can cross over—even if they wanted to.'"
16.27: The man begged again: 'Then please send Lazarus to my dad's house—
16.28: I got five brothers! I don't want them endin' up here too!'
16.29: But Abraham said, 'They got Moses and the prophets—let them read that.'
16.30: He replied, 'Nah, but if somebody rose from the dead and showed up, then they'd listen.'
16.31: Abraham shut it down: 'If they ain't listenin' to the Scriptures, they ain't gon' be convinced—even if somebody came back from the grave.'"

17.1: Then Jesus told His crew, "Ain't no way offenses ain't gon' happen, but woe to the one who brings 'em."
17.2: "It'd be better for that person to get a concrete necklace and tossed in the ocean than to trip up one of these lil' ones."
17.3: "Y'all better check yourselves. If your brother do you dirty, call it out. If he turn it around, forgive him."
17.4: "Even if he mess up seven times in one day, and come back sayin' 'My bad' each time—you still gotta forgive him."
17.5: Then the apostles told the Lord, "Yo, boost our faith!"
17.6: Jesus said, "If y'all had faith the size of a mustard seed, you could tell a mulberry tree, 'Get up and jump in the sea,' and it would listen."
17.7: "Suppose one of y'all got a servant workin' the fields or takin' care of sheep. When he come in, do you say, 'Sit down and eat with me'?"
17.8: "Nah, you tell him, 'Fix my plate, serve me first. Then you can eat after I'm good.'"
17.9: "You don't thank him just for doin' what he was supposed to, do you?"
17.10: "Same with y'all—when you do what God told you to do, just say, 'We just servants. We did what we had to do, nothin' extra.'"
17.11: On the way to Jerusalem, Jesus was walkin' between Samaria and Galilee.
17.12: As He came into a village, ten men with leprosy stood from a distance.
17.13: They shouted, "Jesus! Master! Show us some mercy!"
17.14: When He saw them, He said, "Go on and show yourselves to the priests." And while they were walkin', boom—they got healed.
17.15: One of 'em, when he saw he was healed, turned back, shoutin' loud and givin' God praise.
17.16: He dropped down at Jesus' feet, thankin' Him. And yep—he was a Samaritan.
17.17: Jesus was like, "Hold up—weren't ten of y'all healed? Where the other nine at?"
17.18: "Ain't nobody else come back to give God glory but this outsider?"
17.19: Then Jesus told him, "Get up and go. Yo faith made you whole."
17.20: The Pharisees asked Jesus, "When the kingdom of God comin'?" And He said, "It ain't gon' be something you can spot with your eyes."
17.21: "You ain't gon' hear folks sayin', 'It's over here!' or 'There it go!'—'cause the kingdom of God? It's already in y'all."
17.22: Then He turned to His disciples and said, "The time comin' when y'all gon' wish you could see just one day with the Son of Man, but you won't."
17.23: "Folks gon' be tellin' y'all, 'Look here!' or 'Look there!' Don't fall for it. Don't follow 'em."
17.24: "When I come back, it'll be loud and clear—like lightning shootin' across the whole sky."
17.25: "But first, I gotta go through a whole lotta pain and get rejected by this generation."
17.26: "Just like it was in Noah's time, it'll be the same when the Son of Man returns."
17.27: "Folks was eatin', drinkin', gettin' married—then boom—Noah got in the ark and the flood came and wiped 'em out."
17.28: "Same with Lot's time—folks was chillin', buyin' stuff, plantin', and buildin'."
17.29: "Then Lot dipped outta Sodom, and fire and brimstone came down and destroyed it all."
17.30: "That's exactly how it'll be when I show back up."
17.31: "When that day hits, don't go back for your stuff. If you on the roof or in the field—leave it."
17.33: "If you try to save your life, you gon' lose it. But if you let go, you'll find it."
17.34: "I'm tellin' y'all—on that night, two folks gon' be in the bed—one taken, one left."
17.35: "Two women grindin' at the mill—one taken, one left."
17.36: "Two men in the field—one taken, one left."
17.37: The disciples asked, "Where at, Lord?" And He said, "Where the body at, that's where the vultures gon' be."

18.1: Jesus told 'em a parable so folks would know—they gotta pray all the time and not give up.
18.2: He said, 'There was a judge in a city who ain't fear God and ain't care 'bout nobody.'
18.3: A widow in that same city kept coming to him like, 'Please give me justice against the one doin' me wrong.'
18.4: At first, he ain't wanna do nothin'. But after a while he was like, 'Even though I don't fear God or care 'bout people—'
18.5: 'This woman won't stop botherin' me. I'ma give her what she want so she don't keep wearin' me out!'
18.6: Then Jesus said, 'Y'all hear what that crooked judge said, right?'
18.7: 'So you think God ain't gon' step in for His chosen ones that cry to Him day and night? You think He ain't payin' attention?'
18.8: 'I'm tellin' y'all, He gon' move quick for them. But when the Son of Man show up, is He even gon' find folks still standin' in faith?'
18.9: Then Jesus told another parable, this time for folks who was feelin' themselves and lookin' down on others.
18.10: 'Two men went up to the temple to pray—one was a Pharisee, the other a tax man.'
18.11: The Pharisee stood up proud and prayed like, 'God, I thank You I ain't like these other folks—crooks, cheaters, wildin' out—or even like this tax man right here.'
18.12: 'I fast twice a week and I give my tenth on everything I got.'
18.13: But the tax man? He stood way in the back. Wouldn't even look up. He just beat on his chest like, 'God, have mercy on me. I'm a mess.'
18.14: 'Let me tell y'all—*that* man went home made right with God, not the Pharisee. If you lift yourself up, you gon' get humbled. But if you humble yourself, God gon' lift you up.'
18.15: People started bringing babies to Jesus so He could touch 'em. But when the disciples saw it, they tried to shut it down.
18.16: Jesus was like, 'Nah, let the kids come to Me. Don't block 'em. The kingdom of God belong to folks like them.'
18.17: 'For real, I'm tellin' y'all—if you don't receive God's kingdom like a little kid, you ain't gettin' in.'
18.18: Then a ruler came up and asked Him, 'Good Teacher, what I gotta do to get eternal life?'
18.19: Jesus said, 'Why you callin' Me good? Ain't nobody truly good except God alone.'
18.20: 'You know the commandments—don't cheat, don't kill, don't steal, don't lie on nobody, and honor your folks.'
18.21: The man said, 'I been doin' all that since I was young.'
18.22: Jesus heard him and said, 'One thing you still missin'. Sell what you got, give that money to the poor—you'll have treasure in heaven. Then come follow Me.'
18.23: When he heard that, he got real sad 'cause he had stacks. He was real rich.
18.24: Jesus saw that and said, 'Man, it's hard for rich folks to get in the kingdom of God.'
18.25: 'It's easier for a camel to squeeze through a needle's eye than for a rich man to step into God's kingdom.'
18.26: Folks heard that and said, 'Well then, who *can* be saved?'
18.27: Jesus said, 'What's impossible for people is possible with God.'
18.28: Then Peter said, 'Look, we left everything to follow You.'
18.29: Jesus replied, 'Believe Me, ain't nobody that gave up house, parents, siblings, wife, or kids for God's kingdom—'
18.30: 'Who won't get way more in this life, and eternal life in the next one.'
18.31: Then He pulled the Twelve aside and said, 'Look, we headed to Jerusalem. Everything the prophets wrote 'bout the Son of Man gon' go down.'
18.32: 'He gon' be handed over to the outsiders. They gon' clown Him, disrespect Him, and spit on Him.'
18.33: 'They gon' beat Him and kill Him. But on the third day, He gon' rise.'
18.34: But the disciples ain't get it. It was like the meaning was hidden—they ain't understand what He meant.
18.35: As Jesus was gettin' close to Jericho, a blind man was sittin' by the road, beggin'.
18.36: He heard a crowd passin' by and asked what was goin' on.
18.37: They told him, 'Jesus of Nazareth is passin' through.'
18.38: So he started shoutin', 'Jesus! Son of David! Have mercy on me!'
18.39: The folks up front told him to hush, but he just yelled louder, 'SON OF DAVID, HAVE MERCY ON ME!'
18.40: Jesus stopped and told 'em to bring the man over. When he got close, Jesus asked him—
18.41: 'What you want Me to do for you?' He said, 'Lord, I just wanna see again.'
18.42: Jesus said, 'Aight then—receive your sight. Your faith done made you whole.'
18.43: And just like that, the man could see. He followed Jesus, praisin' God. And everybody who saw it gave God the glory too.

19.1: Jesus rolled through Jericho, just passin' through.
19.2: There was this dude named Zacchaeus. He was a big boss in the tax game — and he had money.
19.3: He was tryna see who Jesus was, but the crowd was too thick, and he was mad short.
19.4: So he ran up ahead and climbed up a sycamore tree, just to catch a glimpse of Jesus as He walked by.
19.5: When Jesus got to that spot, He looked up and said, "Zacchaeus! Come on down quick, I'm stayin' at your crib today."
19.6: Zacchaeus didn't waste no time — he hopped down and welcomed Him with joy.
19.7: But folks was hatin'. They was like, "Wow… He really gon' eat with a sinner?"
19.8: Zacchaeus stood up and told the Lord, "Look, Lord — I'm givin' half my stuff to the poor. And if I scammed anybody, I'ma pay 'em back four times over."
19.9: Jesus said, "Salvation done pulled up to this house today. This man one of Abraham's kids too."
19.10: "The Son of Man came to look for the lost and bring 'em back home."
19.11: While folks was listenin', Jesus dropped another parable — they thought God's kingdom was about to show up any minute.
19.12: He said, "A nobleman went off to a far land to get crowned king and come back.
19.13: Before he dipped, he called ten of his workers, gave 'em each a mina, and said, 'Run it up 'til I get back.'
19.14: But the folks back home hated him. They even sent a squad after him like, 'We don't want this man ruling us.'
19.15: When he came back as king, he called them same workers to see what they did with his money.
19.16: The first one came up like, 'Boss, your one mina made ten more!'
19.17: The king said, 'Bet! You did your thing with a lil' bit, now you run ten cities.'
19.18: Then the second one said, 'Boss, I flipped your one mina into five.'
19.19: He told him, 'You got five cities then.'
19.20: Then another came and said, 'Here's your mina. I wrapped it up in a handkerchief and kept it.'
19.21: 'I was shook, 'cause you a hard man. You collect where you ain't deposit, and you harvest where you ain't even sowed.'
19.22: The king said, 'I'ma judge you off your own words. You knew I don't play.
19.23: So why ain't you at least put it in the bank? I coulda got interest when I came back!'
19.24: Then he told the folks standin' around, 'Take that mina from him and give it to the one with ten.'
19.25: They were like, 'But he already got ten!'
19.26: He said, 'Yeah, and the ones that got, gon' get more. But if you ain't got nothin', even what little you got gon' get snatched.'
19.27: 'Now bring all them haters who didn't want me as king — line 'em up and get rid of 'em right here in front of me.'"
19.28: After that, Jesus kept it pushin' toward Jerusalem.
19.29: When He got close to Bethphage and Bethany, near Mount Olives, He sent two disciples ahead.
19.30: He told 'em, "Go into that village across from y'all. Soon as you walk in, you'll see a young donkey tied up that ain't never been rode. Untie it and bring it to Me.
19.31: If somebody asks what y'all doin', just say, 'The Lord need it.'"
19.32: They went out and found everything exactly how Jesus said it would be.
19.33: As they was untyin' the donkey, the owners said, "Why y'all takin' our donkey?"
19.35: So they brought it back to Jesus, threw their coats on it, and helped Him up on it.
19.36: As Jesus rode, folks laid their coats down on the road in front of Him.
19.37: When He got close to the Mount of Olives, the whole crowd of disciples started turnin' up, shoutin' praise to God for all the wild miracles they had seen:
19.38: "Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven and glory way up high!"
19.39: Some Pharisees in the crowd said, "Teacher, tell your people to chill."
19.40: But Jesus was like, "If they get quiet, these rocks gon' start shoutin'!"
19.41: As He got closer and saw the city, He started cryin'.
19.42: He said, "If only you knew, especially today, what coulda brought you peace. But now your eyes too blind to see it.
19.43: The time's comin' when your enemies gon' trap you in — they gon' circle you, close in from every side,
19.44: and tear you and your kids down to the ground. Not one stone gon' be left standing. 'Cause you ain't realize when God showed up for you."
19.45: Jesus pulled up to the temple and started flippin' tables — kickin' out the folks buyin' and sellin'.
19.46: He told 'em, "It's written, 'My house is a place of prayer.' But y'all turned it into a straight-up trap house."
19.47: He kept teachin' in the temple every day. But the priests, the religious leaders, and the big names was tryna find a way to kill Him.
19.48: They couldn't touch Him though, 'cause the people was glued to every word He said.

20.1: One day while Jesus was up in the temple, teachin' the people and preachin' the Good News, the chief priests, scribes, and elders pulled up on Him.
20.2: They said, "Aight, tell us—who gave you the right to do all this? Who told you you could move like this?"
20.3: Jesus said, "Lemme ask y'all somethin' first. You answer Me, then I'll answer you."
20.4: "That baptism John was doin'—was that straight from heaven or some man-made stuff?"
20.5: They started whisperin' to each other, "If we say it came from heaven, He gon' ask, 'So why ain't y'all believe him then?'"
20.6: "But if we say it was from man, the people might stone us, 'cause they all swear John was a real prophet."
20.7: So they played it safe and said, "We don't know where it came from."
20.8: Jesus said, "Cool then. Since y'all don't wanna answer Me, I ain't tellin' y'all where I get my authority either."
20.9: Then Jesus started tellin' the people a story. He said, "A man planted a vineyard, rented it out to some folks, and dipped out to another country for a long while."
20.10: "When it was time to get some fruit, he sent a servant to collect what's his. But the renters beat that man up and sent him back with nothin'."
20.11: "So he sent another one. They beat him down too, treated him dirty, and sent him away empty-handed."
20.12: "Then a third one got sent—and they did him even worse. Beat him up and straight tossed him out."
20.13: "So the owner said, 'What now? I'ma send my son, the one I love. Maybe they'll respect him.'"
20.14: "But when they saw the son comin', they said, 'Yo, that's the heir! Let's kill him so we can snatch what's his!'"
20.15: "They dragged him out the vineyard and killed him. Now tell me—what y'all think the owner gon' do?"
20.16: "He gon' show up, destroy those wicked folks, and hand the vineyard over to some new folks." When the crowd heard that, they said, "Nah, that can't be!"
20.17: But Jesus looked at them and said, "Then what that verse mean that say: 'The stone the builders threw out Done turned into the cornerstone'?"
20.18: "If you trip over that stone, you gon' break. But if that stone fall on you? You gettin' crushed."
20.19: Right then, the religious leaders wanted to lay hands on Jesus, but they was scared of the crowd. They knew that story was a shot at them.
20.20: They kept watchin' Him and sent some fake righteous folks to trap Him up, tryin' to get Him caught up with the governor.
20.21: They asked, "Teacher, we know you solid, and you teach straight truth. You don't play favorites, and you always speak on what God really want. So here's our question…"
20.22: "Is it legal for us to pay taxes to Caesar or not?"
20.23: Jesus peeped their game and said, "Why y'all tryna play Me?"
20.24: "Show me a denarius. Whose face and name on that coin?" They said, "Caesar's."
20.25: He told 'em, "Then give Caesar what's his, and give God what's His."
20.26: They couldn't trap Him on that one. Matter fact, they was shook by how slick He answered. So they shut up real quick.
20.27: Then some Sadducees came up. These the ones who don't believe in no resurrection.
20.28: They said, "Teacher, Moses told us that if a man die and leave no kids, his brother should marry the widow and raise up children for him."
20.29: "So there was this family—seven brothers. The first one married a woman, then died with no kids."
20.30: "Then the second brother married her, but he died too, no kids."
20.31: "Same with the third… and all the way down. All seven married her, and none left any kids."
20.33: "So in the resurrection, whose wife she gon' be? All seven had her."
20.34: Jesus said, "People in this world get married and stuff."
20.35: "But in the resurrection? The ones worthy of that new life don't marry or get married."
20.36: "They don't die no more either. They like the angels and are God's children now, since they part of the resurrection."
20.37: "And Moses even showed the resurrection is real—remember that burning bush? He called the Lord 'the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.'"
20.38: "He ain't the God of the dead, but of the livin'. Everybody live to Him."
20.39: Some scribes spoke up like, "Teacher, that was solid."
20.40: After that, they ain't even try to question Him no more.
20.41: Then Jesus asked, "How they say Christ is David's son?"
20.42: "David himself said in the Psalms: 'The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand,"
20.43: "Till I put your enemies under your feet.'"
20.44: "If David called Him 'Lord,' how's He his son?"
20.45: Then Jesus turned to His disciples with the whole crowd listenin' and said,
20.46: "Y'all better watch out for them scribes. They love walkin' round in fancy clothes, want folks to greet 'em big in public, and always tryna snatch the best seats."
20.47: "They rob widows and act holy with them long prayers. But trust Me—they gon' get hit with the worst judgment."

21.1: Jesus looked up and saw the rich folks droppin' their money off at the treasury.
21.2: Then He saw this one poor widow come through and toss in two little coins.
21.3: He said, "Listen up—I'm tellin' y'all the truth: this poor widow gave more than all of them."
21.4: "They gave outta their extra, but she gave all she had, even though she barely had nothin'. That was her whole livelihood."
21.5: Some folks started talkin' about how fly the temple looked, all decked out in stones and big-time donations.
21.6: Jesus said, "Y'all see all this? The time comin' when not one of these stones gon' be left sittin' on top of another. It's all comin' down."
21.7: They asked Him, "Teacher, when all this supposed to happen? And what signs should we look for so we know it's about to go down?"
21.8: Jesus said, "Y'all better stay sharp so nobody runs game on you. A lotta folks gon' come sayin' they Me, or sayin', 'The time's here!' Don't chase after them."
21.9: "And when y'all hear about wars and chaos, don't panic. That stuff gotta happen first, but that ain't the end yet."
21.10: Then He said, "Nation gon' rise up against nation, and kingdom against kingdom."
21.11: "There'll be big earthquakes all over, famines, diseases, and some wild signs from the sky."
21.12: "But before all that, they gon' snatch y'all up and come for you. They'll lock y'all up, drag you to court, and bring you before kings and bosses—all 'cause of My name."
21.13: "But that's gon' be y'all's moment to speak up. Use that time to testify."
21.14: "Don't stress about what you gon' say beforehand."
21.15: "I'ma give y'all the words and the wisdom, and your haters won't be able to argue with you or shut you down."
21.16: "Even your folks—parents, siblings, cousins, and so-called friends—gon' turn on you. Some of y'all might even get killed."
21.17: "Everybody gon' hate on you 'cause you roll with Me."
21.18: "But not even one hair from your head gon' be lost."
21.19: "If y'all hold it down and stay steady, you'll keep your soul intact."
21.20: "When you see Jerusalem surrounded by soldiers, just know—it's about to get real. That's the sign it's about to be destroyed."
21.21: "If you in Judea, run for the hills. If you in the city, dip out. And if you outside, don't even try to go back in."
21.22: "These are payback days, so everything the scriptures said gotta happen."
21.23: "But woe to the pregnant women and nursing moms in those days! It's gon' be heavy out here—mad stress and anger fallin' on this people."
21.24: "They gon' die by the sword, and the rest gon' get snatched and dragged off to other nations. And Jerusalem? Gentiles gon' trample it till their time is up."
21.25: "You gon' see wild signs in the sun, moon, and stars. Down here, nations gon' be trippin', confused and scared, with the oceans actin' up."
21.26: "Folks' hearts gon' fail 'em 'cause of fear and what's comin' down on the world. Even the heavens gon' be shakin'."
21.27: "Then they gon' see the Son of Man showin' up in a cloud, flexin' with power and glory."
21.28: "When you see all this startin' to happen, stand up tall and lift your head. Your rescue is comin'."
21.29: Then Jesus dropped a parable: "Look at the fig tree—and all the other trees too."
21.30: "When they start buddin', y'all already know summer's around the corner."
21.31: "Same thing here—when you see all this go down, know the kingdom of God is pullin' up."
21.32: "For real, I'm tellin' y'all, this generation won't pass before all this happens."
21.33: "The sky and earth might pass away, but My words? They ain't goin' nowhere."
21.34: "Y'all better watch yourselves. Don't get caught up partyin', drinkin', or stressin' over life's problems. Don't let that Day catch you slippin'."
21.35: "It's gon' drop on everybody across the whole earth, like a trap."
21.36: "So stay woke. Keep prayin' all the time, askin' that you can dodge all that's comin' and still be able to stand before the Son of Man."
21.37: Every day, Jesus was teachin' in the temple. But at night, He'd head out and chill on Mount Olivet.
21.38: And every mornin', the people pulled up early to the temple just to hear Him speak.

22.1: The Feast of Unleavened Bread was comin' up—the one they call Passover.
22.2: The chief priests and the scribes was tryna figure out how to kill Jesus, but they was scared of the crowd.
22.3: Then Satan slid in on Judas—yep, the one called Iscariot—one of the Twelve.
22.4: Judas went and linked up with the chief priests and temple guards, tryin' to work out how he could set Jesus up for them.
22.5: They were hype about it, and promised to break him off with some money.
22.6: So Judas agreed, and started lookin' for the right moment to hand Jesus over—when the crowd wasn't around.
22.7: Then the day came when they had to kill the Passover lamb—Feast of Unleavened Bread.
22.8: Jesus told Peter and John, "Go on and get the Passover meal ready for us to eat."
22.9: They asked, "Where you want us to do it?"
22.10: He said, "Soon as y'all get in the city, a man carryin' a water jug gon' meet y'all. Follow him to the house he go into."
22.11: "Then ask the man of the house, 'The Teacher wanna know where the guest room at, so He can eat Passover with His disciples.'"
22.12: "He gon' show y'all a big upstairs room already set up. That's where y'all need to get it ready."
22.13: So they left, and it went down exactly how Jesus said. They got everything set for Passover.
22.14: When the time came, Jesus sat down with the Twelve.
22.15: He told them, "I been waitin' to eat this Passover meal with y'all before I go through this suffering."
22.16: "I'm tellin' y'all now—I ain't eatin' this meal again till it get fulfilled in God's kingdom."
22.17: Then He took a cup, gave thanks, and said, "Pass this around to each other."
22.18: "I won't be drinkin' wine again till God's kingdom come."
22.19: Then He took some bread, gave thanks, broke it, and passed it to them sayin', "This My body, given up for y'all. Eat it to remember Me."
22.20: After supper, He took another cup and said, "This cup right here is the new deal—My blood bein' poured out for y'all."
22.21: "But look, the one who's gon' betray Me? His hand on this table with Mine."
22.22: "The Son of Man gotta go like it's been written. But still—woe to the one who betray Him!"
22.23: Then they all started whisperin' and wonderin', "Who would even do somethin' like that?"
22.24: Then they started arguin' about who among them was the top dawg.
22.25: Jesus said, "Look, kings out here be actin' like bosses, and the big shots get called 'benefactors.'"
22.26: "But that ain't how y'all gon' move. The greatest one among y'all should act like the youngest. And the one in charge? Be the one servin'."
22.27: "Who's bigger? The one eatin' at the table or the one servin' food? Ain't it the one at the table? But I'm here servin'—right in front of y'all."
22.28: "Y'all been rockin' with Me through all My struggles."
22.29: "So I'ma bless y'all with a kingdom, just like My Father blessed Me."
22.30: "Y'all gon' eat and drink at My table in the kingdom, sittin' on thrones, judgin' the twelve tribes of Israel."
22.31: Then Jesus said, "Simon, Simon—listen. Satan been askin' for you, tryna shake you up like wheat in a sifter."
22.32: "But I prayed for you—that your faith won't fall apart. And when you bounce back, go strengthen your brothers."
22.33: Peter said, "Lord, I'm down for You! I'll go to jail or even die with You!"
22.34: Jesus said, "Boy, I'm tellin' you straight up—before that rooster crows today, you gon' deny three times that you even know Me."
22.35: Then Jesus asked, "Back when I sent y'all out without a money bag, backpack, or sandals—did y'all lack anything?" They said, "Nah, we ain't miss nothin'."
22.36: Then Jesus said, "But now, if you got a money bag, better bring it. Same with a travel bag. And if you ain't got a sword, sell your jacket and buy one."
22.37: "'Cause I'm tellin' y'all, what's written 'bout Me gotta come true: 'He was counted among the rebels.' What's about to go down with Me—it's comin' to a close."
22.38: They said, "Lord, look—we got two swords right here." And Jesus said, "Aight, that's enough."
22.39: Jesus left out and went to the Mount of Olives like He usually did. His disciples followed Him.
22.40: When they got there, He told them, "Y'all pray so you don't fall into temptation."
22.41: He went off a lil' ways from them—just a stone's throw—and dropped to His knees and prayed.
22.42: He said, "Father, if You willin', take this cup from Me. But still—not what I want, but what You want."
22.43: Then an angel from heaven came through and gave Him strength.
22.44: And He was in deep agony, prayin' even harder. His sweat was fallin' like big drops of blood hittin' the ground.
22.45: When He got up from prayin', He went back to the disciples and saw them knocked out—sleepin' from sorrow.
22.46: He said, "Why y'all sleepin'? Get up and pray, so you don't fall into temptation."
22.47: While He was still talkin', here come a crowd. And at the front was Judas—yeah, one of the Twelve—comin' up to kiss Jesus.
22.48: But Jesus said, "For real, Judas? You betrayin' the Son of Man with a kiss?"
22.49: When the disciples saw what was 'bout to go down, they asked, "Lord, should we pull out the swords?"
22.50: And one of them sliced the high priest's servant and took off his right ear.
22.51: But Jesus said, "Nah, let it be." Then He touched the man's ear and healed him.
22.52: Jesus turned to the chief priests, temple guards, and elders who came to snatch Him, and said, "Y'all came at Me like I'm some kind of thug—with swords and clubs?"
22.53: "I been with y'all every day in the temple, and y'all ain't touch Me. But this here? This y'all's hour. This darkness? That's y'all's lane."
22.54: They grabbed Jesus and took Him to the high priest's house. Peter followed—but he stayed at a distance.
22.55: Folks had started a fire in the courtyard and were sittin' around it. Peter sat with them.
22.56: A servant girl looked hard at him and said, "He was with Jesus too."
22.57: But Peter denied it: "Girl, I don't even know Him."
22.58: A little later, somebody else saw him and said, "You one of them." Peter said, "Man, I am not!"
22.59: After about an hour, another dude said, "Look, he gotta be one of them—he from Galilee too."
22.60: Peter said, "Man, I don't know what you talkin' about!" And while he was still talkin', the rooster crowed.
22.61: Jesus turned and looked straight at Peter. Then Peter remembered what Jesus had told him: "Before the rooster crows, you gon' deny Me three times."
22.62: Peter dipped out and cried his eyes out.
22.63: The men holdin' Jesus started clownin' Him and beatin' on Him.
22.64: They blindfolded Him, smacked Him up, and said, "Prophesy! Tell us who hit You!"
22.65: And they kept talkin' reckless, blasphemous stuff to Him.
22.66: When the sun came up, the elders, chief priests, and scribes all got together. They brought Jesus to their council and said,
22.67: "If You the Messiah, tell us." Jesus said, "If I told y'all, y'all wouldn't believe Me."
22.68: "And if I asked y'all a question, y'all wouldn't answer or let Me go."
22.69: "But from now on, the Son of Man gon' be sittin' at God's right hand, holdin' all power."
22.70: Then they all said, "So You the Son of God?" And Jesus said, "Y'all said it."
22.71: They said, "We don't need no more witnesses—we heard it with our own ears!"

23.1: Then the whole crowd got up and took Jesus to Pilate.
23.2: They started snitchin', sayin', "This man out here messin' up the people, tellin' folks not to pay taxes to Caesar and claimin' He the Messiah—a whole King."
23.3: Pilate asked Him, "You the King of the Jews?" Jesus said, "You said it."
23.4: Pilate turned to the priests and the crowd and said, "I don't see nothin' wrong with this man."
23.5: But they turned up even more: "He stirrin' up everybody! Teachin' all over Judea—started in Galilee and now He here!"
23.6: When Pilate heard "Galilee," he asked if Jesus was from there.
23.7: And when he found out Jesus was under Herod's rule, he sent Him over to Herod, who happened to be in town too.
23.8: Herod was hyped to see Jesus. He'd been tryna meet Him for a minute, hopin' to see a miracle.
23.9: He hit Jesus with a bunch of questions, but Jesus ain't say a word.
23.10: The priests and scribes kept hollerin' accusations at Him.
23.11: Then Herod and his crew clowned Jesus, dressed Him up in a fancy robe, mocked Him, and sent Him back to Pilate.
23.12: That day, Herod and Pilate went from beefin' to bein' boys—they became cool off Jesus' situation.
23.13: Pilate called everybody back together—priests, leaders, and the people.
23.14: He said, "Y'all brought this man to me, sayin' He was stirrin' up trouble. But I looked into it, and He ain't done nothin' wrong."
23.15: "Herod ain't find nothin' either—He ain't done nothin' to deserve death."
23.16: "So I'ma just rough Him up a bit and let Him go."
23.17: (Pilate had to release somebody during the feast.)
23.18: But they all shouted, "Nah! Get rid of Him! Give us Barabbas!"
23.19: Barabbas had been locked up for starting riots in the city—and for murder.
23.20: Pilate tried again, wantin' to let Jesus go.
23.21: But they screamed louder: "Crucify Him! Crucify Him!"
23.22: A third time, Pilate said, "Why? What'd He do? He ain't done nothin' to deserve death! I'ma just punish Him and let Him go."
23.23: But they wasn't havin' it. They kept yellin' for Him to be crucified—and the priests backed 'em up.
23.24: So Pilate gave in and gave the order they wanted.
23.25: He let Barabbas go—the dude locked up for murder and rebellion—and handed Jesus over to be crucified.
23.26: As they led Jesus away, they grabbed a man named Simon from Cyrene, who was comin' in from the country, and made him carry Jesus' cross.
23.27: A crowd followed, including women cryin' and mournin'.
23.28: Jesus turned and said, "Daughters of Jerusalem, don't cry for Me. Cry for y'all selves and your kids."
23.29: "The time comin' when folks gon' say, 'Blessed are the women who ain't had no kids.'"
23.30: "They gon' say to the mountains, 'Fall on us,' and to the hills, 'Hide us.'"
23.31: "If they do this when the tree still green, what's gon' happen when it's dry?"
23.32: Two other men, criminals, were being taken out with Him to be executed.
23.33: When they got to a place called Calvary, they crucified Jesus there, with the criminals—one on His right, one on His left.
23.34: Jesus said, "Father, forgive them. They don't even know what they doin'." And they rolled dice for His clothes.
23.35: The people just stood there watchin'. The leaders mocked Him, sayin', "He saved others—let Him save Himself if He really God's chosen."
23.36: The soldiers joined in, givin' Him sour wine.
23.37: They said, "If You the King of the Jews, save Yourself."
23.38: There was a sign above Him that said: "THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS."
23.39: One of the criminals hangin' there mocked Him: "Ain't You the Messiah? Save Yourself and us!"
23.40: But the other one snapped back, "You don't fear God? You about to die too!"
23.41: "We gettin' what we deserve. But this man ain't done nothin' wrong."
23.42: Then he said to Jesus, "Lord, remember me when You get to Your kingdom."
23.43: Jesus said, "Today, you gon' be with Me in Paradise."
23.44: Around noon, everything went dark across the land 'til about 3 PM.
23.45: The sun just stopped shinin', and the temple curtain tore straight down the middle.
23.46: Jesus shouted, "Father, into Your hands I give My spirit!" And after He said that, He took His last breath.
23.47: The Roman soldier saw it all and said, "This really was a righteous man!"
23.48: Everybody who came to watch saw what happened, beat their chests in grief, and went home.
23.49: But Jesus' people—His crew and the women who had followed Him from Galilee—stood at a distance, watchin' it all go down.
23.50: A man named Joseph showed up. He was on the council—a good dude who stood for what's right.
23.51: He hadn't agreed with what the others did. He was from Arimathea and was waitin' on God's kingdom too.
23.52: He went to Pilate and asked for Jesus' body.
23.53: He took the body down, wrapped it in linen, and placed it in a tomb cut out the rock—nobody had ever used it before.
23.54: It was the Preparation Day, and the Sabbath was comin' in quick.
23.55: The women who came with Jesus from Galilee followed behind and saw the tomb and how the body was laid.
23.56: Then they went home and got spices and oils ready. But they chilled on the Sabbath like the commandment said.

24.1: Real early Sunday morning, the women came through with the spices they had prepared.
24.2: But when they got to the tomb, that stone was already rolled out the way.
24.3: They went inside, but Jesus' body was gone.
24.4: While they was tryna figure out what happened, two men popped up rockin' fit-for-heaven drip—shinin' bright.
24.5: The women got shook, bowed down, but the men said, "Why y'all lookin' for the livin' in a graveyard?"
24.6: "He ain't here—He got up! Don't y'all remember what He said back in Galilee?"
24.7: "'The Son of Man gotta get handed over to sinful folks, get crucified, and rise up on the third day.'"
24.8: Then they remembered exactly what He had told them.
24.9: They booked it back from the tomb and told the eleven and everybody else what went down.
24.10: The ones who pulled up were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary (James' mama), and some other sisters too.
24.11: But the men thought they was trippin'—talkin' wild—and didn't believe 'em.
24.12: Peter, though, took off runnin' to the tomb. He peeked in, saw the linen cloths layin' there, and left lookin' shook, tryin' to piece it all together.
24.13: That same day, two of Jesus' crew were walkin' to a village called Emmaus, about seven miles out from Jerusalem.
24.14: They was talkin' back and forth about everything that just went down.
24.15: While they was goin' back and forth, Jesus Himself rolled up and started walkin' with 'em.
24.16: But they ain't recognize Him—they was too caught up.
24.17: Jesus said, "What y'all talkin' 'bout that got y'all lookin' so down?"
24.18: One of them, Cleopas, said, "You new in town or somethin'? You don't know what just happened?"
24.19: Jesus played along like, "What happened?" They said, "The stuff about Jesus from Nazareth—He was a prophet, powerful in what He said and what He did, straight from God."
24.20: "But the priests and leaders handed Him over, and He got sentenced to death and crucified."
24.21: "We thought He was the one who'd free Israel. But now it's been three days since He died."
24.22: "And some women from our squad had us shook—they hit the tomb early…"
24.23: "They didn't find His body but said they saw angels who told 'em He was alive."
24.24: "Some of us went to check, and yep—it was just like the women said. But nobody saw Him."
24.25: Then Jesus said, "Y'all slow to catch on and believe what the prophets said!"
24.26: "Wasn't it necessary for the Christ to go through all that and then step into glory?"
24.27: And starting with Moses and all the Prophets, He broke it all down to them—how the Scriptures was all pointin' to Him.
24.28: They got close to the village, and Jesus acted like He was gonna keep goin'.
24.29: But they was like, "Nah, stay with us. It's gettin' late." So He came in with them.
24.30: When they sat down to eat, He took the bread, blessed it, broke it, and passed it out.
24.31: And BAM—their eyes opened and they realized it was Him! Then just like that, He vanished.
24.32: They said, "Bruh! Didn't our hearts burn when He was talkin' on the road and breakin' down Scripture?"
24.33: So they got up right then, ran back to Jerusalem, and found the eleven and the others.
24.34: The crew was like, "The Lord really is alive—He showed up to Simon!"
24.35: Then the two told their story from the road—and how they realized it was Jesus when He broke the bread.
24.36: While they was still talkin', Jesus Himself pulled up in the room and said, "Peace, y'all."
24.37: They was shook—thought they was seein' a ghost.
24.38: Jesus said, "Why y'all trippin'? What's got y'all doubting?"
24.39: "Look at My hands and feet—it's really Me. Touch Me. Ghosts don't have skin and bones like this."
24.40: Then He showed 'em His hands and feet.
24.41: They still couldn't believe it—not 'cause they doubted, but 'cause it was too good to be true. So Jesus said, "Y'all got any food?"
24.42: They gave Him some broiled fish and honeycomb.
24.43: He ate it right there in front of 'em.
24.44: Then He said, "Remember what I told y'all back when I was still walkin' with you—that everything in Moses' Law, the Prophets, and Psalms about Me had to happen?"
24.45: Then He opened their minds so they could understand the Scriptures.
24.46: He said, "Look, the Bible already said it—the Christ had to suffer, rise up on the third day…"
24.47: "And that repentance and forgiveness would be preached in His name to all nations, startin' right here in Jerusalem."
24.48: "Y'all are the ones who saw it go down—you My witnesses."
24.49: "Now hold tight in Jerusalem 'til y'all get that promise from the Father—the power from on high."
24.50: Then He took them out near Bethany, raised His hands, and blessed them.
24.51: While He was blessin' 'em, He started floatin'—taken up to heaven.
24.52: They dropped to worship, then went back to Jerusalem turnt up with joy.
24.53: And every day, they stayed at the temple, praisin' and blessin' God. Amen.
